[[Image:AlecOgletree2013rams.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Ogletree with the Rams in 2013]]
Head coach [[Jeff Fisher]] named Ogletree a starting outside linebacker to start the regular season, alongside [[Will Witherspoon]] and middle linebacker [[James Laurinaitis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: St. Louis Rams Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/LAR |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> He made his professional regular season debut and first career start in the [[2013 St. Louis Rams|St. Louis Rams']] season-opener against the [[2013 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]] and recorded seven solo tackles and forced a fumble in their 27–24 victory. Ogletree made his first career regular season tackle on tight end [[Jim Dray]] after a ten-yard reception by Dray in the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 1-2013: Arizona Cardinals @ St. Louis Rams |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013090810/2013/REG1/cardinals@rams |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 13, 2013, Ogletree recorded ten combined tackles (seven solo), deflected a pass, forced a fumble, and returned his first career interception for a touchdown during a 38–14 win at the [[2013 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]] in Week 6. He intercepted a pass by quarterback [[T. J. Yates]], that was intended for tight end [[Garrett Graham]], and returned it for a 98-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 6-2013: St. Louis Rams @ Houston Texans |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013101303/2013/REG6/rams@texans |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 12, he collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (ten solo) and broke up a pass in the Rams' 42–21 victory against the [[2013 Chicago Bears|Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alec Ogletree (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alecogletree/2540143/gamelogs?season=2013 |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 8, 2013, Ogletree recorded nine combined tackles (eight solo) and made his first career sack during a 30–10 loss at the [[2013 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]] in Week 14. Ogletree made his first a career sack on quarterback [[Carson Palmer]] for a seven-yard loss in the third quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 14-2013: St. Louis Rams @ Arizona Cardinals |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013120810/2013/REG14/rams@cardinals |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in [[2013 NFL season|2013]] with 117 combined tackles (94 solo), ten pass deflections, six forced fumbles, 1.5 sacks, an interception, and a touchdown in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alec Ogletree (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alecogletree/2540143/careerstats |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2013.htm |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2014====
On January 29, 2014, the St. Louis Rams announced the decision to fire defensive coordinator [[Tim Walton (American football)|Tim Walton]] after finishing 15th in the league in overall defense during his lone season with the Rams in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 29, 2014 |title=Rams fire defensive coordinator Tim Walton |url=https://www.komu.com/news/rams-fire-defensive-coordinator-tim-walton/ |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=komu.com}}</ref> Ogletree entered training camp slated as the starting weakside linebacker. Head coach Jeff Fisher named Ogletree and [[Jo-Lonn Dunbar]] the starting outside linebackers to begin the regular season, along with middle linebacker James Laurinaitis.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2014 |title=2014 Rams Depth Chart: Robinson At Backup |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2014/9/2/6100137/rams-depth-chart-greg-robinson-backup |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=turfshowtimes.com}}</ref>

In Week 3, he collected a season-high ten solo tackles during a 34–31 loss to the [[2014 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys]]. On November 9, 2014, Ogletree made seven combined tackles, a season-high three pass deflections, and an interception during a 31–14 loss at the [[2014 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]] in Week 10. The following week, Ogletree collected a season-high 13 combined tackles (ten solo), two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Peyton Manning]] during a 22–7 win against the [[2014 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]] in Week 11.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 11-2014: Denver Broncos @ St. Louis Rams |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014111607/2014/REG11/broncos@rams |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He started all 16 games in 2014 and finished the season with 111 combined tackles (85 solo), a career-high 12 passes defensed, four forced fumbles, and two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Ogletree 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OgleAl00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015====
Head coach Jeff Fisher retained Ogletree as the starting weakside linebacker to begin the regular season. He started alongside middle linebacker James Laurinaitis and strongside linebacker [[Akeem Ayers]].<ref name="p488">{{Cite web |last=Dobozy |first=Frank |date=2015-09-06 |title=2015 Rams: Roster, Depth Chart & Practice Squad |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2015/9/6/9269923/2015-st-louis-rams-53-man-roster-depth-chart-practice-squad |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=Turf Show Times}}</ref> In Week 2, he collected a season-high 16 combined tackles (eight solo) during a 24–10 loss at the [[2015 Washington Redskins|Washington Redskins]]. On September 27, 2015, Ogletree made nine combined tackles and a season-high two sacks in the Rams' 12–6 loss to the [[2015 Pittsburgh Steelers|Pittsburgh Steelers]]. Ogletree sacked quarterback [[Ben Roethlisberger]] for a nine-yard loss in the third quarter and sacked backup quarterback [[Michael Vick]] in the fourth quarter to earn his first multi-sack game of his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 3-2015: Pittsburgh Steelers @ St. Louis Rams |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015092705/2015/REG3/steelers@rams |access-date=July 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 4, 2015, Ogletree recorded ten combined tackles (nine solo) before exiting during the second half of the Rams' 24–22 victory at the [[2015 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]] due to an ankle injury. After the game, head coach Jeff Fisher stated Ogletree's ankle would require surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Injuries: Rams' Alec Ogletree requires ankle surgery |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/injuries-rams-alec-ogletree-requires-ankle-surgery-0ap3000000548783 |access-date=July 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 27, 2015, the St. Louis Rams placed Ogletree on [[injured reserve]] with a designation to return due to a broken [[fibula]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lyons |first=Joe |date=October 27, 2015 |title=Rams report: Ogletree placed on IR in hopes of a December return |work=StLToday.com |url=http://www.stltoday.com/sports/football/professional/rams-report-ogletree-placed-on-ir-in-hopes-of-a/article_1e4f59dc-57a2-525d-a8a0-0d0e0a1a7deb.html |access-date=November 30, 2015}}</ref> Ogletree finished the [[2015 NFL season|2015]] season with 42 combined tackles (27 solo) and two sacks in four games and four starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Ogletree 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OgleAl00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2016====
During the offseason, the St. Louis Rams officially moved to [[Los Angeles]]. On February 24, 2016, head coach Jeff Fisher announced that Ogletree would move from [[weakside linebacker]] to [[middle linebacker]] following the release of veteran [[James Laurinaitis]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hammond, Rich |date=February 24, 2016 |title=Rams will move Alec Ogletree to middle linebacker to fill void left by cutting James Laurinaitis |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2016/02/24/rams-will-move-alec-ogletree-to-middle-linebacker-to-fill-void-left-by-cutting-james-laurinaitis/ |access-date=July 7, 2018 |website=ocregister.com}}</ref> On May 2, 2016, the Los Angeles Rams exercised Ogletree's fifth-year option on his rookie contract. Under the fifth-year option, Ogletree received $8.36 million and remained with the Rams for the [[2016 NFL season|2016 season]].<ref name="spotrac" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wagoner |first=Nick |date=May 2, 2016 |title=Rams pick up fifth-year options on Tavon Austin, Alec Ogletree |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/203650/rams-pick-up-fifth-year-options-on-tavon-austin-alec-ogletree |access-date=November 26, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Head coach Jeff Fisher officially named Ogletree the starting middle linebacker to start the regular season.
<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2016 |title=2016 LA Rams Week 1 Depth Chart Projection |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2016/9/6/12812998/2016-la-rams-week-1-depth-chart-projection-53-man-roster |access-date=July 7, 2018 |website=turfshowtimes.com}}</ref>

He started in the [[2016 Los Angeles Rams|Los Angeles Rams']] season-opener at the [[2016 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]] and collected a season-high 11 solo tackles, assisted on a tackle, and deflected a pass during a 28–0 loss. On November 13, 2016, Ogletree made nine combined tackles, a season-high two pass deflections, and an interception during a 9–6 victory at the [[2016 New York Jets|New York Jets]]. Ogletree intercepted a pass attempt by quarterback [[Bryce Petty]], that was initially intended for wide receiver [[Quincy Enunwa]], and sealed the Rams' victory in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 10-2016: Los Angeles Rams @ New York Jets |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2016111304/2016/REG10/rams@jets |access-date=July 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 13, he collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (four solo) in the Rams' 26–10 loss at the [[2016 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]]. On December 12, 2016, the Los Angeles Rams fired head coach [[Jeff Fisher]] after the Rams fell to a 4–9 record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 12, 2016 |title=Los Angeles Rams fire head coach Jeff Fisher |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/los-angeles-rams-fire-head-coach-jeff-fisher-0ap3000000755854 |access-date=July 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 15, 2016, Ogletree recorded seven combined tackles, two pass deflections, and made an interception as the Rams lost 24–3 at the [[2016 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] Week 15. He intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Russell Wilson]], that was originally intended for wide receiver [[Jermaine Kearse]], in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 15-2016: Los Angeles Rams @ Seattle Seahawks |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2016121500/2016/REG15/rams@seahawks |access-date=July 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He started in all 16 games in 2016 and recorded a career-high 136 combined tackles (98 solo), 11 pass deflections, two interceptions, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Ogletree 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OgleAl00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Ogletree finished with the seventh most combined tackles in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Defense |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/defense.htm |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2017====
The Los Angeles Rams hired [[Wade Phillips]] as their new defensive coordinator and installed his base [[3-4 defense]]. Head coach [[Sean McVay]] officially named Ogletree and [[Mark Barron]] the starting inside linebackers to begin the regular season, along with starting outside linebackers [[Connor Barwin]] and [[Robert Quinn (American football)|Robert Quinn]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kremenjas, Sosa |date=September 5, 2017 |title=LA Rams Unofficial Week 1 53-Man Depth Chart |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2017/9/5/16257522/la-rams-nfl-depth-chart |access-date=July 8, 2018 |website=turfshowtimes.com}}</ref>

On October 12, 2017, the Los Angeles Rams signed Ogletree to a four-year, $42.75 million contract extension with $21.36 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $8 million.<ref name="spotrac" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2017 |title=Alec Ogletree, Rams agree on 4-year, $42M extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/alec-ogletree-rams-agree-on-4-year-42m-extension-0ap3000000860556 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 11, he collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (11 solo) and a pass deflection during a 24–7 loss at the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings]]. On December 3, 2017, Ogletree made a solo tackle, a pass deflection, and returned an interception for his second career touchdown during a 32–16 win at the [[2017 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]]. He intercepted a pass attempt by quarterback [[Blaine Gabbert]], that was intended for running back [[D. J. Foster]], and returned it for a 41-yard touchdown during the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 13-2017: Los Angeles Rams @ Arizona Cardinals |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2017120311/2017/REG13/rams@cardinals |access-date=July 8, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Head coach Sean McVay chose to rest Ogletree, along with the starters, for the Rams' Week 17 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers as the Rams had already clinched the NFC West division with an 11–4 record. He finished the [[2017 NFL season|2017 season]] with 95 combined tackles (63 solo), ten pass deflections, two sacks, an interception, a forced fumble, and a touchdown in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Ogletree 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OgleAl00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The [[2017 Los Angeles Rams|Los Angeles Rams]] finished first in the NFC West with an 11–5 record and clinched a wildcard berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Los Angeles Rams Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/ram/2017.htm |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 6, 2018, Ogletree started in his first career playoff game and recorded five solo tackles during a 26–13 loss to the [[2017 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] in the NFC Wildcard Game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Atlanta Falcons at Los Angeles Rams - January 6th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801060ram.htm |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
====2018====
On March 7, 2018, the Rams agreed to trade Ogletree and a 2019 seventh-round pick to the [[New York Giants]] in exchange for a fourth and a sixth round pick in the [[2018 NFL draft]]. The fourth round pick was used to select [[John Franklin-Myers]], while the sixth round pick was used to select [[John Kelly (running back)|John Kelly]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra, Kevin |date=March 7, 2018 |title=Rams to trade Alec Ogletree to Giants for two picks |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-to-trade-alec-ogletree-to-giants-for-two-picks-0ap3000000920018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The deal became official on March 14, 2018, at the start of the new league year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=March 14, 2018 |title=New York Giants acquire LB Alec Ogletree via trade |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-acquire-LB-Alec-Ogletree-via-trade/01e02b0e-bde4-4e3e-9ec4-7a854616f48b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315133754/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-acquire-LB-Alec-Ogletree-via-trade/01e02b0e-bde4-4e3e-9ec4-7a854616f48b |archive-date=March 15, 2018 |access-date=March 15, 2018}}</ref>
In Week 13 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Ogletree intercepted [[Chase Daniel]] twice including a Pick Six in a 30–27 overtime win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at New York Giants - December 2nd, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812020nyg.htm |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2019====
During training camp, Ogletree switched from No. 52 to No. 47 after trading with fellow linebacker [[Jake Carlock]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burks |first=Serena |date=August 6, 2019 |title=Giants' Alec Ogletree now wears No. 47: What led to the change? |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2019/08/06/new-york-giants-alec-ogletree-now-wears-no-47-what-led-change/ |access-date=September 6, 2020 |website=giantswire.usatoday.com}}</ref>
[[File:Giants Captains 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Ogletree alongside other Giants' team captains in a game against the [[2019 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]] ]]
In week 6 against the [[New England Patriots]], Ogletree recorded 12 tackles and sacked [[Tom Brady]] once in the 35–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 October 2019 |title=Patriots force 4 turnovers, beat Giants 35-14 to reach 6-0 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127917 |access-date=10 October 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>
In week 12 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Ogletree recorded his first interception of the season off [[Mitch Trubisky]] in the 19–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2019 |title=Mack, Robinson lead Bears to 19-14 win over Giants |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127914 |access-date=November 24, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

On February 26, 2020, Ogletree was released by the Giants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |title=Giants release Alec Ogletree and Kareem Martin |url=https://www.giants.com/news/alec-ogletree-kareem-martin-released-2020-free-agency |access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On September 10, 2020, Ogletree was signed to the [[New York Jets]] [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=September 10, 2020 |title=Jets add Alec Ogletree to practice squad |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/10/jets-add-alec-ogletree-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=September 10, 2020 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 19, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg, Ethan |date=September 19, 2020 |title=Jets Sign LB Alec Ogletree and Elevate RB Josh Adams and WR Josh Malone |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-lb-alec-ogletree-and-elevate-rb-josh-adams-and-wr-josh-malone |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was released on October 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg, Ethan |date=October 10, 2020 |title=Jets Activate RB Le'Veon Bell from IR, Sign OL Jimmy Murray to Active Roster |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-rb-le-veon-bell-from-ir-sign-ol-jimmy-murray-to-active-roster |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On August 4, 2021, Ogletree signed with the [[Chicago Bears]], reuniting him with former [[Los Angeles Rams]] [[linebacker]] [[Robert Quinn (American football)|Robert Quinn]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=August 4, 2021 |title=Roster Move: Bears sign veteran linebacker Ogletree |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-sign-veteran-linebacker-ogletree |website=ChicagoBears.com |access-date=August 5, 2021 |archive-date=August 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804222752/https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-sign-veteran-linebacker-ogletree |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ogletree started all 16 games for Chicago in 2021, tallying 87 combined tackles, four pass deflections, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Ogletree 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OgleAl00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On June 21, 2023, Ogletree announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Former Bulldog Alec Ogletree Announces Retirement|url=https://www.si.com/college/georgia/news/former-georgia-bulldog-alec-ogletree-announces-retirement-from-nfl|access-date=June 21, 2023|newspaper=Sports Illustrated|language=en}}</ref>

'''Aldon Jacarus Ramon Smith''' (September 25, 1989 – June 13, 2026) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for six seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] with the seventh overall pick in the [[2011 NFL draft]]. Smith was a first-team [[All-Pro]] and a [[Pro Bowl]] selection as an outside linebacker with the 49ers in 2012. He also played at defensive end for the [[Oakland Raiders]] and [[Dallas Cowboys]].

==Early life==
Aldon Jacarus Ramon Smith was born on September 25, 1989, in [[Kansas City, Missouri]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Richardson|first=Jerrell |date=November 6, 2012 |title=49ers Figuring Out How To Keep Aldon Smith On The Field |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/49ers-figuring-out-how-to-keep-aldon-smith-on-the-field/ |access-date=2026-06-14 |publisher=[[KOVR]]|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121116011854/http://sacramento.cbslocal.com:80/2012/11/06/49ers-figuring-out-how-to-keep-aldon-smith-on-the-field/|archive-date=November 16, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended [[Raytown Senior High School|Raytown High School]] in [[Raytown, Missouri]], where he played for the Raytown Bluejays [[high school football]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith – Football Recruiting – Player Profiles – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/52523/aldon-smith |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> As a senior, Smith recorded 60 tackles, 21 tackles for loss, and 12 sacks, while adding seven forced fumbles, one blocked punt, and a safety on defense, while on offense, he caught 34 passes for 570 yards and four touchdowns as a [[tight end]].{{Cn|date=June 2026}}

Considered only a three-star recruit by the ''[[Rivals.com]]'' (now just known as Rivals) recruiting network, Smith was considered the No. 5 overall prospect (any position) in the state of Missouri as well as the No. 27 strongside defensive end in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith, 2008 Strongside Defensive End |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2008/aldon-smith-23367 |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He chose Mizzou over [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]], and [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith Recruit Interests |url=https://247sports.com/Recruitment/Aldon-Smith-57344/RecruitInterests/ |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Smith played for the [[Missouri Tigers football]] team under head coach [[Gary Pinkel]] while attending the [[University of Missouri]] from 2008 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aldon-smith-1.html |access-date=May 3, 2011 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Missouri Tigers Coaches |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/missouri/ |access-date=June 13, 2011 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> After being redshirted as a freshman in 2008, Smith started 11 of 13 games at defensive end in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aldon Smith|url=http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/smith_aldon00.html|work=MUTigers.com|publisher=University of Missouri|access-date=June 24, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120606145410/http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/smith_aldon00.html|archive-date=June 6, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He finished the season with 60 tackles and 11 [[quarterback sack|sacks]]. Smith was named the [[Big 12]] Defensive Freshman of the Year and a first-team [[Freshman All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2009 |title=2009 All-Big 12 Football Awards Announced |url=http://big12sports.com/news/2009/12/1/204842329.aspx |access-date=June 14, 2026 |publisher=Big 12 Conference|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229064937/http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=204842329|archive-date=December 29, 2010 |language=en|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2010, he played in nine games, recording 48 tackles and six sacks.

After the season, Smith announced that he would forgo his final two years of eligibility and enter the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2011|last=Ubben|first=David |title=Missouri DE Aldon Smith enters NFL Draft |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/24218/missouri-de-aldon-smith-enters-nfl-draft |access-date=January 15, 2011 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110109113134/https://espn.go.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/24218/missouri-de-aldon-smith-enters-nfl-draft|archive-date=January 9, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Playing as a defensive end at Missouri, Smith was considered a "DE/OLB prospect" by most NFL scouts and was considered a strong edge run defender as 4–3 end or 3–4 linebacker.<ref>[http://proprospects.wordpress.com/2011/01/19/aldon-smith-scouting-report/ Aldon Smith Scouting Report « PRO Prospects]</ref> Many scouts compared him to [[DeMarcus Ware]].{{Cn|date=June 2026}} Prior to the [[2011 NFL draft]], Smith was projected to be selected in the mid-late first round by mock draft analysis.{{Cn|date=June 2026}}

===San Francisco 49ers===
====2011 season====
The [[San Francisco 49ers]] drafted Smith in the first round with the seventh overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |access-date=May 3, 2011 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Smith did not start but made his NFL debut in the season-opening 33–17 victory over the [[2011 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], recording a pass deflection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers – September 11th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109110sfo.htm |access-date=September 14, 2011 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[2011 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], Smith recorded five tackles and his first 1.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] on [[Michael Vick]] in the narrow 24–23 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Philadelphia Eagles – October 2nd, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110020phi.htm |access-date=October 4, 2011 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Over the next two weeks, Smith would win the [[Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week]] in victories against the [[2011 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and [[2011 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]]. After a strong October, Smith became the first 49ers player since linebacker [[Patrick Willis]] in [[2007 NFL season|2007]] to earn the NFL Rookie of the Month award; Smith recorded 13 tackles and 6.5 sacks, including one that forced a [[Safety (American and Canadian football score)|safety]] as he helped the 49ers to a 6–1 record.{{Cn|date=June 2026}}

During a week 15 of the season  20–3 victory over the [[2011 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Smith recorded four tackles and 2.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sando |first=Mike |date=December 20, 2011 |title=Aldon Smith has shot at rookie sack record |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcwest/post/_/id/54907/aldon-smith-has-shot-at-rookie-sack-record |access-date=December 29, 2011 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He also surpassed [[Charles Haley]] for the 49ers record for most sacks by a rookie in a single season with 13.0.<ref name=rookie-sack>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2011 |title=Smith earns 49ers' rookie sack record<!-- Bot generated title --> |url=http://www.csnbayarea.com/blog/niners-talk/post/Smith-earns-49ers-rookie-sack-record?blockID=615542&feedID=2539 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730055252/http://www.csnbayarea.com/blog/niners-talk/post/Smith-earns-49ers-rookie-sack-record?blockID=615542&feedID=2539 |archive-date=July 30, 2012 |access-date=December 29, 2011 |website=CSN Bay Area}}</ref>

He finished his rookie year with 37 total tackles, 14 sacks, four pass deflections, two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery in 16 games.<ref name=2011-stats>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl04/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=January 28, 2012 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was half a sack shy of tying the all-time rookie sack record held by defensive end [[Jevon Kearse]] despite not starting a single game in his rookie season. Smith was named Defensive Rookie of the Year by [[Pro Football Writers of America]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pomin |first=Ernie |date=January 19, 2012 |title=49ers Aldon Smith Named 2011 PFW/PFWA Defensive Rookie of the Year |url=https://bayarea.sbnation.com/san-francisco-49ers/2012/1/19/2718993/49ers-aldon-smith-named-2011-pfw-pfwa-defensive-rookie-of-the-year |access-date=January 21, 2012 |website=SB Nation Bay Area |language=en}}</ref> and finished second to [[Von Miller]] for the [[Associated Press]] [[NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sando |first=Mike |date=January 5, 2012 |title=49ers' Aldon Smith top defensive rookie? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcwest/post/_/id/56489/49ers-aldon-smith-top-defensive-rookie |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Smith was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2011.htm |access-date=February 7, 2012 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

[[File:Aldon Smith blocks Ed Dickson.jpg|thumb|200px|left|Smith takes on block by tight end [[Ed Dickson]] in [[Super Bowl XLVII]]]]
Smith finished his second professional season with 19.5 sacks, 66 tackles, three forced fumbles, an interception, and a pass deflection in 16 games and starts. He broke [[Cedrick Hardman]]'s 49er's franchise record of 18 sacks in one season, which Hardman set in 1971, a 14-game NFL season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fucillo |first=David |date=March 9, 2019 |title=Cedrick Hardman, 49ers all-time sack leader, passes away |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2019/3/9/18257624/cedrick-hardman-obituary-49ers-all-time-sack-leader |access-date=March 12, 2019 |website=Niners Nation |language=en|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20190310063651/https://www.ninersnation.com/2019/3/9/18257624/cedrick-hardman-obituary-49ers-all-time-sack-leader|archive-date=March 10, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> The 49ers went on to appear in [[Super Bowl XLVII]]. In the game, Smith had two combined tackles as the 49ers narrowly lost to the [[2012 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] by a score of 34–31.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLVII – San Francisco 49ers vs. Baltimore Ravens – February 3rd, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201302030sfo.htm |access-date=February 14, 2013 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On the [[NFL Network]]'s [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2013]] ranking, players voted Smith as the seventh-best player in the league entering the 2013 season, which made him the second-highest-ever debut and second-highest defensive player on the list, both behind [[J. J. Watt]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2013-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=August 30, 2013 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Smith was voted the San Francisco 49ers MVP in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Corkran |first=Steve |date=January 28, 2013 |title=Super Bowl 2013: Aldon Smith is San Francisco 49ers MVP |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/2013/01/28/super-bowl-2013-aldon-smith-is-san-francisco-49ers-mvp/ |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website=San Jose Mercury News |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505023614/http://www.mercurynews.com/2013/01/28/super-bowl-2013-aldon-smith-is-san-francisco-49ers-mvp/|archive-date=May 5, 2017|url-access=limited|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2013 season====
Smith got off to a fast start in 2013, recording 18 tackles and 4.5 sacks in the first three games. However, on September 20, he was involved in a single-vehicle accident in [[San Jose, California]]. He was subsequently arrested on suspicion of [[driving under the influence]] and possession of marijuana. After a Week 3 27–7 loss to the [[2013 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Smith voluntarily entered a rehabilitation facility, to be put onto the non-football injury list with an indefinite leave of absence.<ref name="Rosenthal">{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=September 22, 2013 |title=Aldon Smith will take indefinite leave of absence |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aldon-smith-will-take-indefinite-leave-of-absence-0ap2000000248867 |access-date=June 14, 2026 |publisher=NFL.com |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130924143321/http://www.nfl.com:80/news/story/0ap2000000248867/article/aldon-smith-will-take-indefinite-leave-of-absence|archive-date=September 24, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Smith missed five games while in rehabilitation. He returned to the team in Week 10 against the [[2013 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]], but in a backup role, and did not start a game until Week 13 against the [[2013 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]]. Smith ended the season strong, finishing with 34 tackles and 8.5 sacks in 11 games and eight starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl04/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=January 25, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Despite his limited playing time, Smith was ranked #33 in the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2014]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2014-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=August 6, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2014 season====
Smith served a nine-game suspension for violating the NFL's substance abuse and personal conduct policies. He was reinstated in Week 11.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |date=November 11, 2014 |title=Aldon Smith returns to the 49ers |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/11/aldon-smith-returns-to-the-49ers/ |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141202024835/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/11/aldon-smith-returns-to-the-49ers/|archive-date=December 2, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 7, 2015, following an arrest for his third DUI, Smith was released by the 49ers.<ref name="PaulGuiterrez">{{Cite web |last=Guiterrez |first=Paul |date=August 7, 2015 |title=Aldon Smith cut by 49ers after latest DUI arrest |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13394571/aldon-smith-released-san-francisco-49ers |access-date=August 14, 2015 |publisher=ESPN |language=en|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20150809141425/https://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/13394571/aldon-smith-released-san-francisco-49ers|archive-date=August 9, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===

Smith made his Raiders debut in the team's season-opening loss to the [[2015 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] and recorded two tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Oakland Raiders – September 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509130rai.htm |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[2015 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], Smith got his first start of the year and finished the 27–20 road victory with two solo tackles and two pass deflections.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Cleveland Browns – September 27th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509270cle.htm |access-date=September 28, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[2015 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], he recorded a season-high six tackles and his first sack of the season as the Raiders narrowly lost on the road by a score of 22–20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Chicago Bears – October 4th, 2015 in Week 10 against the [[2015 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] and finished the 30–14 loss with three tackles and a sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Oakland Raiders – November 15th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511150rai.htm |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Two days later, the ====2016 and 2017 seasons====
On April 4, 2016, Smith re-signed with the Raiders. On October 27, he applied for reinstatement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=La Canfora |first=Jason |date=October 27, 2016 |title=Aldon Smith formally files for reinstatement to the Raiders' active roster |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/aldon-smith-formally-files-for-reinstatement-to-the-raiders-active-roster/ |access-date=June 24, 2026|publisher=CBS Sports |language=en|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20161031151135/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/aldon-smith-formally-files-for-reinstatement-to-the-raiders-active-roster/|archive-date=October 31, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> However, no reinstatement occurred, resulting in Smith sitting out the entire 2016 and 2017 NFL seasons.<ref name="b521">{{cite web | last=Brock | first=Todd | title=Cowboys DE Aldon Smith reinstated by league after 4 years away from field | website=Cowboys Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2020-05-20 | url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2020/05/20/dallas-cowboys-aldon-smith-reinstatement-suspension-defensive-end/ | access-date=December 23, 2024|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20200528093747/https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/2020/05/20/dallas-cowboys-aldon-smith-reinstatement-suspension-defensive-end/|archive-date=May 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following an alleged domestic violence incident, the Raiders released Smith on March 5, 2018.<ref name="Raiders release Aldon Smith">{{Cite web |last=Peterson|first=Gary|title= Raiders release Aldon Smith hours after he reportedly checks into rehab for substance abuse |url=https://www.eastbaytimes.com/2018/03/05/raiders-linebacker-aldon-smith-reportedly-in-rehab-after-domestic-violence-incident/|work=East Bay Times|date=March 5, 2018|access-date=June 24, 2026|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20180616210806/https://www.eastbaytimes.com/2018/03/05/raiders-linebacker-aldon-smith-reportedly-in-rehab-after-domestic-violence-incident/|archive-date=June 16, 2018|url-status=dead|url-access=limited}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On March 14, 2020, it was reported Smith was "in the process" of applying for reinstatement from an indefinite league suspension. He signed a one-year contract with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on April 2, after impressing that organization with his conditioning and size (287 pounds).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=April 1, 2020 |title=Cowboys sign DE Aldon Smith to 1-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28983576/cowboys-agree-1-year-deal-de-aldon-smith-source-says |access-date=April 3, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On May 20, Smith was conditionally reinstated by the NFL and was cleared to take part in the Cowboys' virtual off-season program.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=May 20, 2020 |title=Aldon Smith reinstated by NFL, set to join Cowboys |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aldon-smith-reinstated-by-nfl-set-to-join-cowboys?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |access-date=May 20, 2020 |website=[[NFL.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys' Aldon Smith 'grateful' to be reinstated by NFL|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29205274/cowboys-aldon-smith-grateful-reinstated-nfl|publisher=ESPN|date=May 21, 2020|access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref>

During the season-opening 20–17 road loss to the [[2020 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]] on ''Sunday Night Football'', Smith played in a regular season game for the first time since November 15, 2015. He tied for a team-high 11 tackles (one for a loss), had his first sack of the season, and had two quarterback hits on [[Jared Goff]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Los Angeles Rams – September 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009130ram.htm |access-date=September 14, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[2020 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], Smith sacked [[Russell Wilson]] thrice, had two tackles for loss, four quarterback hits, and a pass deflection in the 38–31 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Seattle Seahawks – September 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009270sea.htm |access-date=September 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> After posting four sacks in the first three games, Smith's production decreased considerably in the following weeks (tallying only one more sack) and he also was limited with a knee injury. His time on the field was reduced in favor of the Cowboys playing defensive end [[Randy Gregory]]. During a Week 14 30–7 road victory over the [[2020 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]], Smith recovered a fumble lost by running back [[Trayveon Williams]] and returned it 78 yards (fifth longest in franchise history) for his first NFL touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Cincinnati Bengals – December 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012130cin.htm |access-date=December 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Smith finished the 2020 season with 53 tackles (four for loss), five sacks (second on the team), 35 quarterback pressures (second on the team), two pass deflections, and two fumble recoveries in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aldon Smith 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl04/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=January 4, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 Dallas Cowboys Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/dal/2020.htm |access-date=February 8, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On April 15, 2021, Smith signed a one-year contract with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=April 15, 2021 |title=Seahawks Sign DE Aldon Smith |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-de-aldon-smith |access-date=April 16, 2021 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> On August 11, he was released.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 11, 2021 |title=Seahawks Sign LB Lakiem Williams, Release DE Aldon Smith |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-lb-lakiem-williams-waive-de-aldon-smith |access-date=August 23, 2021 |website=Seahawks.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Retirement===
Following his release from jail on October 24, 2023, Smith stated that he was "done with (foot)ball".<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonald |first=Jerry |date=October 24, 2023 |title=Former 49er Aldon Smith is out of jail, says he's done with football |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2023/10/24/former-49er-aldon-smith-is-out-of-jail-says-hes-done-with-football|access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=Mercury News |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==

=== Legal issues ===

==== 2012 ====
On January 28, 2012, Smith was arrested for [[driving under the influence]] in [[Miami Beach, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Branch |first=Eric |date=January 29, 2012 |title=49ers' star rookie Aldon Smith accused of DUI |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/49ers-star-rookie-Aldon-Smith-accused-of-DUI-2792517.php |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=The San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref>

On June 30, Smith was believed to have suffered stab wounds when attempting to break up a fight at a party at his [[Santa Clara County]] residence. Two other people were shot in the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2012 |title=Aldon Smith reportedly stabbed at party; 49ers: Injuries 'minor' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aldon-smith-reportedly-stabbed-at-party-49ers-injuries-minor-09000d5d82a3f82f |access-date=August 2, 2012 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 9, 2013, Smith was charged with "three felony counts of illegal possession of an assault weapon" relating to the stabbing incident. The charges were later reduced to misdemeanors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=October 9, 2013 |title=Aldon Smith charged with assault weapon possession |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aldon-smith-charged-with-assault-weapon-possession-0ap2000000259850 |access-date=June 24, 2026 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131009222427/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000259850/article/aldon-smith-charged-with-assault-weapon-possession|archive-date=October 9, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==== 2013 ====
On September 20, 2013, Smith was involved in a single-vehicle accident in San Jose, California. He was subsequently arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence and possession of marijuana. After a Week 3 27–7 loss to the [[2013 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Smith voluntarily entered a rehabilitation facility, to be put onto the non-football injury list with an indefinite leave of absence.<ref name="Rosenthal" />

==== 2014 ====
On April 13, 2014, Smith was detained and arrested following an incident at the [[Los Angeles International Airport]] in which he became belligerent and uncooperative with a [[TSA]] agent, who alleged Smith claimed he was carrying a bomb.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reyes |first=Lorenzo |date=April 14, 2014 |title=Aldon Smith arrested on false bomb report charge |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/49ers/2014/04/13/49ers-linebacker-aldon-smith-arrested-at-airport/7683243/ |access-date=June 24, 2026 |website=USA Today|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20140416221009/http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/49ers/2014/04/13/49ers-linebacker-aldon-smith-arrested-at-airport/7683243/|archive-date=April 16, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> After interviews revealed that Smith did not clearly state he was carrying a bomb, the [[Los Angeles City Attorney]] decided to drop the charges. Smith was suspended for nine games in the 2014 season.

==== 2015 ====
On August 6, 2015, Smith was arrested in Santa Clara, California, for an alleged hit and run after driving under the influence, and vandalism charges.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guiterrez |first=Paul |date=August 7, 2015 |title=49ers' Aldon Smith arrested in hit and run, DUI |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13393290/aldon-smith-san-francisco-49ers-arrested-hit-run-dui |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He was released by the 49ers the next day as a result.<ref name="PaulGuiterrez" />

==== 2017 ====
On March 9, 2017, Smith was a passenger with a friend driving to Smith's house at 12:00 am, when the [[San Francisco Police Department]] found out both Smith and the driver were under the influence after hitting a police car. Even though Smith was not the driver, both Smith and his friend were detained by the San Francisco Police Department for questioning. The next day, Smith and his friend were released and no arrests were made.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 9, 2017 |title=NFL's Aldon Smith Detained By Police ... Drunk Passenger In Cop Car Crash |url=http://www.tmz.com/2017/03/09/aldon-smith-oakland-raiders-detained-cops/ |access-date=March 14, 2017 |website=TMZ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 9, 2017 |title=Aldon Smith Denies Wrongdoing ... 'I'm Not a Badass Criminal, I'm a Good Person' (VIDEO) |url=http://www.tmz.com/2017/03/09/aldon-smith-denies-wrongdoing-im-not-a-bad-ass-criminal-im-a-good-person/ |access-date=March 14, 2017 |website=TMZ}}</ref>

On September 23, 2017, it was announced that Smith had agreed to plead [[no contest]] to hit and run in the 2015 incident in exchange for the DUI charges being dropped. He was sentenced to 20 days in jail. During his sentence, Smith was ordered to attend a [[Residential treatment center|treatment facility]] and undergo [[anger management]] training classes. After his release, Smith was prohibited from entering any bars or other establishments where alcohol is the primary commodity being sold.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2017 |title=NFL's Aldon Smith Strikes Plea Deal In DUI Hit and Run Case |url=http://www.tmz.com/2017/09/22/aldon-smith-hit-and-run-dui-plea-deal/ |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=TMZ}}</ref>

==== 2018 ====
On March 3, 2018, a woman called the police from Smith's home and reported that he had consumed multiple bottles of [[tequila]] and then bit her wrists. Smith reportedly fled the home before police arrived.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lee|first=Vic|url=https://abc7news.com/post/former-raider-aldon-smith-bails-out-after-domestic-violence-arrest/3182184/|title=Former Oakland Raiders LB Aldon Smith bails out after turning himself in to SFPD|work=ABC7News.com|publisher=[[KGO-TV]]|date=March 6, 2018|access-date=June 24, 2026|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20180309091741/http://abc7news.com/sports/former-raider-aldon-smith-bailed-out-after-domestic-violence-arrest/3182184/|archive-date=March 9, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 23, Smith was arrested for violation of a court order, where he was ordered to stay away from a woman he assaulted earlier in the month. The woman was revealed to be Smith's fiancée. This picked up from the previous incident that occurred on March 3, where Smith pleaded not guilty on four misdemeanor counts, including: domestic violence, assault with force likely to produce great bodily injury, false imprisonment, and vandalism.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 23, 2018 |title=Aldon Smith arrested for violating court order |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/22884767/former-san-francisco-49er-oakland-raiders-player-aldon-smith-arrested-again |access-date=March 23, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On April 8, he was arrested for violations of conditions to his bail.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 8, 2018 |title=Aldon Smith arrested again |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/23077347/aldon-smith-arrested-again-held-500000-bond |access-date=April 8, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==== 2019 ====
On June 11, 2019, Smith was stopped by police in Mission, Kansas for a traffic violation, and later arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 11, 2019 |title=Aldon Smith arrested. Yet again. |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2019/6/12/18662435/aldon-smith-arrest-49ers-dui-wth |access-date=June 14, 2019 |website=WDSU.com}}</ref><ref name="y914">{{cite web | url=https://www.kansascity.com/news/local/crime/article231423583.html|title=Former NFL star Aldon Smith arrested on suspicion of DUI in Mission, Kansas|last=Cronkleton|first=Robert A.|work=The Kansas City Star|date=June 11, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2026|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20190616071833/https://www.kansascity.com/news/local/crime/article231423583.html|archive-date=June 16, 2019|url-status=live|url-access=limited}}</ref>

==== 2021 ====
On April 19, 2021, the [[St. Bernard Parish, Louisiana|St. Bernard Parish]], Louisiana Sheriff's Office issued an arrest warrant for Smith for second-degree battery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 19, 2021 |title=St. Bernard Parish: Arrest warrant issued for Seattle Seahawks defensive end accused of battery |url=https://www.wdsu.com/article/sheriff-seattle-seahawks-defensive-end-wanted-for-battery-in-st-bernard-parish/36165328 |access-date=April 19, 2021 |website=WDSU.com}}</ref> Smith surrendered two days later and was released on a $25,000 bond with an arraignment scheduled for July 14.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henderson |first=Brady |date=April 21, 2021 |title=Seattle Seahawks' Aldon Smith booked on battery charge in Louisiana |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31302571/seattle-seahawks-aldon-smith-turns-alleged-assault-louisiana |access-date=November 26, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On December 7, Smith was arrested for driving under the influence in [[San Mateo County]], California.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=2021-12-07 |title=Aldon Smith is arrested for DUI causing injury, a felony |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/aldon-smith-is-arrested-for-dui-causing-injury-a-felony |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> On April 7, 2023, he was sentenced to a year in jail after pleading no contest to a felony charge stemming from this incident.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Wilton |date=April 7, 2023 |title=Aldon Smith Sentenced to One Year in Jail After Pleading No Contest to DUI, per Report |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2023/04/08/aldon-smith-sentenced-one-year-jail-no-contest-dui-report |access-date=April 7, 2023 |website=si.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Posey |first=Kyle |date=April 7, 2023 |title=Friday night thread: Aldon Smith sentenced to 1 year in jail after DUI charge |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2023/4/7/23674887/aldon-smith-christian-mccaffrey-richie-james-49ers |access-date=April 7, 2023 |website=Niners Nation |language=en}}</ref>

=== Death ===
On June 13, 2026, a friend found Smith unresponsive in his vehicle after they had delivered food to a homeless shelter.<ref name=Chron-death>{{cite news |first1=Matthias |last1=Gafni |first2=Noah |last2=Furtado |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/49ers/article/aldon-smith-49ers-talented-troubled-ex-pass-22304314.php |title=Inside Aldon Smith's final hours: Ex-49er's friend tried to revive him in truck |newspaper=San Francisco Chronicle |date=June 14, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260615233627/https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/49ers/article/aldon-smith-49ers-talented-troubled-ex-pass-22304314.php|archive-date=June 15, 2026 }}</ref> He was pronounced dead later that day at the age of 36 at [[Good Samaritan Hospital (San Jose)|Good Samaritan Hospital]] in [[San Jose, California]].<ref name=Chron-death/><ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2026-06-13 |title=Aldon Smith, ex-49ers star and franchise's single-season sacks record-holder, dies at age 36 |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nfl/san-francisco-49ers/aldon-smith-death/1943171/ |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California }}</ref>

'''Alex Albright''' (born January 29, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College Eagles]].

==Early life==
Albright is a 2006 graduate of [[St. Xavier High School (Cincinnati)|St. Xavier High School]] in [[Cincinnati]]. He played [[defensive end]] in [[American football|football]]<ref>{{cite news|title=St. Xavier (OH)'s Steven Daniels Is Latest Bomber-Turned-Eagle|first=Brian|last=Favat|work=[[SB Nation]]|publisher=Vox Media|date=December 16, 2010|accessdate=April 15, 2023|url=https://www.bcinterruption.com/2010/12/16/1878921/st-xavier-oh-s-steven-daniels-is-latest-bomber-turned-eagle}}</ref> and as a senior he registered 83 tackles with 12 sacks, while helping his team win the 2005 Division I state title. At the end of the season, he was named All-State, All-Southwest Ohio first-team, received the Greater Catholic League South Player of the Year award and played in the Ohio North-South Classic. He also was a starter on the school's [[basketball]] team that advanced to the 2005 Division I state championship game.

==College career==
He accepted a [[American football|football]] scholarship from [[Boston College]] and played in all 13 games as a true freshman [[defensive end]]. In his sophomore season, he missed the final two games after breaking his left forearm, but still received All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) honorable mention, finishing with 38 tackles, a team-leading 8.5 sacks and 10 tackles-for-losses. The 
next year, he played in only two games after suffering a neck injury and being [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]].

As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] junior he started in seven games and recorded 32 tackles, with eight for losses. As a fifth-year senior he was named team captain, but played in only eight games after breaking his leg, finishing the year with 30 tackles, nine tackles-for-losses, 3.5 sacks and an [[interception]].

==Professional career==
Albright wasn't selected in the [[2011 NFL draft]] because of his injury history and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Get To Know a UFA: Alex Albright|url=http://www.nbcdfw.com/blogs/blue-star/Get-To-Know-a-UFA-Alex-Albright-127467178.html|publisher=[[KXAS]]|access-date=11 August 2011}}</ref> As a rookie, he was converted to [[outside linebacker]], where he was a backup in all 16 games, finishing third on the team with 14 [[special teams]] tackles.

In the [[2012 NFL season|2012 preseason]], injuries forced the team to play him at [[tight end]] for a few days, so that the offense could get its normal practice reps. During the regular season, he showed his versatility backing up all four [[linebacker]] positions and starting two games at [[inside linebacker]] after [[Ernie Sims]] got hurt.<ref>{{cite web|title=Garrett Applauds Ryan's Work Getting New Defenders Ready|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2012/12/17/garrett-applauds-ryan%E2%80%99s-work-getting-new-defenders-ready|publisher=DallasCowboys.com|access-date=11 August 2011|archive-date=7 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307225023/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2012/12/17/garrett-applauds-ryan%E2%80%99s-work-getting-new-defenders-ready|url-status=dead}}</ref> He finished the season third on the team with 17 [[special teams]] tackles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Rundown: Albright's Versatility Will Aid 4-3 Switch|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2013/02/05/roster-rundown-albright%E2%80%99s-versatility-will-aid-4-3-switch|publisher=DallasCowboys.com|access-date=11 August 2011|archive-date=3 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200303032049/https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2013/02/05/roster-rundown-albright%E2%80%99s-versatility-will-aid-4-3-switch|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In [[2013 NFL season|2013]], Albright suffered a career ending back injury while playing a preseason game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]]. On August 19 he was waived injured,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/article-DavidHelman/Cowboys-Place-Three-Including-Albright-On-WaivedInjured-List/86c24bf3-6f6c-47d1-a7b6-13da36b17686 |title=Cowboys Place Three, Including Albright, On Waived/Injured List |last=Helman |first=David |date=August 19, 2013 |website=DallasCowboys.com |access-date=August 19, 2013 |archive-date=August 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130822053554/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/article-DavidHelman/Cowboys-Place-Three-Including-Albright-On-WaivedInjured-List/86c24bf3-6f6c-47d1-a7b6-13da36b17686 |url-status=dead }}</ref> before being placed on [[injured reserve]] the next day. He was released from the team on September 10.

'''Alec Tyler Lemon''' (born July 1, 1991) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]] and was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Houston Texans]] in 2013.<ref name="SBNation">{{cite news | last =Bien | first =Louis | title =Undrafted Free Agents 2013: Collin Klein Among 23 New Texans Post-Draft | newspaper =SB Nation| date =April 28, 2013 | url =https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2013/4/28/4278260/2013-nfl-undrafted-free-agents-houston-texans | access-date =April 29, 2013 }}</ref>

Lemon is currently an educator at Glen Burnie High School, Glen Burnie Maryland and the Head Football Coach of the Glen Burnie Gophers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mr. Alec Lemon |url=https://www.glenburniehs.org/apps3/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=1129703&type=u |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=www.glenburniehs.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Lemon attended Arundel Senior High School in [[Gambrills, Maryland]] where he played both offense and defense.<ref name="BleacherReportLemon"/> He set the record for the most receiving yards his senior year with a total of 1,616, while tying the records for touchdowns (23) and receptions (103). He also added 30 tackles, 6 interceptions, and 2 forced fumbles while on the defensive side of the ball.<ref name="BleacherReportLemon"/>

Lemon was also known for playing baseball during high school and recognized as someone who helped the local community as a volunteer for the Arundel School Mentoring Program.<ref name="BleacherReportLemon">{{cite news | last =Stein | first =Matt | title =Alec Lemon: 5 Things You Need To Know About The Syracuse WR | newspaper =Bleacher Report| date =April 26, 2013 | url =https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1612808-alec-lemon-5-things-you-need-to-know-about-the-syracuse-wr | access-date =April 29, 2013 }}</ref> As a senior, he was team captain and a first-team all-state selection by the Associated Press for football.<ref name="BaltimoreSunAaronWilson">{{cite news | last =Wilson | first =Aaron | title =Syracuse WR, Former Arundel Standout Alec Lemon Worked Out For Bills | newspaper =Baltimore Sun | date =April 8, 2013 | url =http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-syracuse-wide-receiver-arundel-alum-alec-lemon-worked-out-for-bills-20130408,0,3282854.story | archive-url =https://archive.today/20130616153220/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-syracuse-wide-receiver-arundel-alum-alec-lemon-worked-out-for-bills-20130408,0,3282854.story | url-status =dead | archive-date =June 16, 2013 | access-date =April 29, 2013 }}</ref>

==College career==
Lemon attended Syracuse University where he played wide receiver. His senior year, he caught 73 passes for 1,074 yards including 7 touchdowns. This earned him an All-Big East Conference selection. This followed up on his junior year where he caught 69 passes for 834 yards and second-team All-Big East honors.<ref name="BaltimoreSunAaronWilson"/> His senior year, he also became the all-time leader in pass receptions for the Orangemen, a title previously held by [[Rob Moore (American football)|Rob Moore]].<ref name="ESPNBigEastBlog"/>

Lemon played in the 2013 [[Senior Bowl]] prior to working out with other NFL prospects at the [[NFL Scouting Combine|NFL Combine]].<ref name="WashingTonPostFormerStar"/>

==Professional career==
Lemon was taken as an undrafted free agent by the Houston Texans following the NFL Draft.  Lemon impressed through the camp and the preseason to make the Texans roster and was placed on injured reserve throughout the 2013 campaign.  Lemon was released from the Texans the following year and was added to the Baltimore Ravens practice squad in 2014.  Following a brief stint with the Saskatchewan Roughriders, Lemon was done with his professional football career.

In 2020, Lemon was named head coach of the Glen Burnie Senior High School football team.  Lemon is also a physical education and life sciences educator at Glen Burnie.  Glen Burnie had not had a winning season in 20 years when Lemon took over.  In his first season, the team went 2–7 while the COVID pandemic continued in 2021; however, in his second season (2022), Glen Burnie finished 5–4, hosted its first playoff game in school history winning 39–7 against Parkville High School before losing to Old Mill in the second round of the playoffs.  In 2023, Lemon led Glen Burnie to a 6–3 regular season record and again dispatched the first-round opponent - Meade High School - by a 28–27 score.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-03 |title=Three Anne Arundel County football teams are trying to break into county's elite behind good coaching, players buying in |url=https://www.capitalgazette.com/sports/high-school/ac-cs-glen-burnie-meade-annapolis-football-print-20231103-zpn2hsgjrbandgrkvie2hdlive-story.html |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=Capital Gazette}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-03 |title=Glen Burnie football outlasts Meade, 28-27, in first round playoff game: 'These kids fight for each other' |url=https://www.capitalgazette.com/sports/high-school/ac-cs-meade-glen-burnie-football-20231104-ti5zcmkmabdithn7rzlyfjdu4q-story.html |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=Capital Gazette}}</ref>

'''Alejandro Villanueva Martín''' (born September 22, 1988) is a Spanish-American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Army Black Knights football|Army Black Knights]] and fulfilled his service commitment after graduation, where he reached the rank of captain. Villanueva also served in the [[75th Ranger Regiment]], earning a [[Bronze Star Medal|Bronze Star]]. After serving three [[tours of duty]] in [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|Afghanistan]], he signed a contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2014, but was waived prior to the season. He then signed with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] and played for them for six seasons until signing with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in 2021 for his final season.

==Early life==
Villanueva was born on [[Naval Air Station Meridian]] in [[Meridian, Mississippi]], to Ignacio Villanueva, a [[Spanish Navy|Spanish Naval]] officer who worked for [[NATO]], and his Spanish wife Matilde Martín.<ref name="tall order"/><ref>{{cite web|title=El motrileño Alejandro Villanueva, de soldado en Afganistán a titular indiscutible en la NFL|url=http://www.ideal.es/granada/deportes/mas-deportes/201510/20/motrileno-alejandro-villanueva-soldado-20151020113115.html|website=ideal.es|access-date=January 16, 2017|language=es-ES|date=October 20, 2015}}</ref> Both his mother and father are over {{convert|6|ft|sigfig=3}} tall. Alejandro is the eldest of the family's four children, including siblings Carmen, [[Iñaki Villanueva|Iñaki]] and Paloma.

During his childhood, he lived in [[Rhode Island]], [[Spain]], and [[Belgium]]. In Spain he learned to play [[rugby union|rugby]], which, for a time, he preferred to football.<ref name="tall order"/> Later when his family moved to Belgium he continued to play rugby at [[SHAPE High School]]. One of his friends from SHAPE was later recruited to play football for the Army Black Knights, and raved about Villanueva to the Army coaches, putting him on their radar.<ref name="long path" /> They kept in touch and Villanueva told him that he was considering attending [[United States Military Academy|West Point]], a school to which he later attended.<ref name="long path">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/page/hotread140522/army-veteran-alejandro-villanueva-pursues-nfl-dream-philadelphia-eagles-three-tours-afghanistan |title=Alejandro Villanueva's long NFL path |author=Ashley Fox |work=ESPN.com |date=May 22, 2014}}</ref>

His brother [[Iñaki Villanueva]] is a professional [[rugby union]] player. He plays with the [[Spain national rugby union team]] and with the [[Spain national rugby sevens team|sevens team]]. He was in the squad that qualified for the [[Rugby sevens at the 2016 Summer Olympics|2016 Olympics]], and he played in the Olympic tournament.

==College career==
[[File:Alejandro Villanueva football.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Villanueva during his 
first class year with Army]]
Villanueva played college football for the Army Black Knights at several positions, including [[left tackle]], [[defensive lineman]], and [[wide receiver]].<ref name="nfl">{{cite web|last=Breer|first=Albert|title=Super Regional Combine: Army veteran giving NFL one last shot|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/super-regional-combine-army-veteran-giving-nfl-one-last-shot-0ap2000000341231|work=NFL.com|publisher=NFL Enterprises|access-date=May 5, 2014|date=April 14, 2014}}</ref> Though originally recruited as a [[tight end]], he played defensive end during his freshman season, mostly on special teams. In his sophomore season offensive line coach John Tice lobbied to have Villanueva converted to an offensive tackle which occurred near the end of his sophomore year. By his junior season he started every game at left tackle. Voted a [[captain (sports)|team captain]] before his senior year, he reluctantly converted once more to become a {{convert|290|lb|kg}} wide receiver; a feature story in the Army football program read, "Already touted as the tallest football player in the country, Villanueva completed the transformation from being an offensive lineman for the past two years, to running routes on the field with the starting offense last Saturday night."<ref name="tall order">{{cite web|last=Volkmann |first=Tim |title=A Tall Order: Things are looking up for Army football |url=http://www.goarmysports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/091209aab.html |work=Army Black Knights Football |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=May 9, 2014 |date=September 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140513023534/http://www.goarmysports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/091209aab.html |archive-date=May 13, 2014 }}</ref> His height, while reported by Army Football in 2009 to be {{convert|6|ft|10|in|m}},<ref name="tall order" /> was given by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2014 as {{convert|6|ft|9|in|m}}.<ref name="Eagles/army" />
