===Tryouts===
Although he went undrafted in the [[2010 NFL draft]], he received a tryout with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] as a tight end, but did not make the team and went back into military service.<ref name="nfl"/> Two years later, he made a second attempt to play in the NFL as a tight end. He was given a tryout and practiced with the [[Chicago Bears]], but was not signed. After finishing his last tour with the [[75th Ranger Regiment]], Villanueva decided to pursue his NFL career again and began working out at [[Savannah State University]]. In March 2014, he paid $245 to attend a regional NFL combine in [[Flowery Branch, Georgia]]. During this time, the NFL held 10 regional combines nationwide and had over 3,000 prospects attend. In April 2014, he was one of 240 prospects invited to the NFL super regional combine in [[Detroit]] and met with representatives from the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref name="path">{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/nfl/story/_/page/hotread140522/army-veteran-alejandro-villanueva-pursues-nfl-dream-philadelphia-eagles-three-tours-afghanistan| title=Alejandro Villanueva's long NFL path| access-date=February 1, 2017| website=ESPN.com| author=Ashley Fox| date=May 22, 2014}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On May 5, 2014, he was signed to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] for an undisclosed contract to play as a [[defensive end]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Eagles sign Alejandro Villanueva, former US Army Ranger, to play defensive end |url=http://www.nj.com/eagles/index.ssf/2014/05/eagles_sign_alejandro_villanueva_former_us_army_ranger_to_play_defensive_end.html |publisher=NJ.com |last=Shorr-Parks|first=Eliot |date=May 5, 2014 |access-date=May 5, 2014}}</ref> His signing marked the second time the Eagles had signed a military veteran in recent years, having previously had [[Chad Hall]], a wide receiver from the [[United States Air Force|Air Force]], as a member of the team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gardner|first=Sam|title=Philadelphia Eagles sign U.S. Army Ranger Alejandro Villanueva|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/nfl/story/philadelphia-eagles-sign-u-s-army-ranger-alejandro-villanueva-050514|work=FOX Sports|publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|access-date=May 7, 2014|date=May 5, 2014}}</ref> Villanueva said that if he did not make an NFL roster, he planned to serve a fourth tour of duty in Afghanistan.<ref name="nbc"/> He commented, "I see this as a win-win situation. Obviously, I'm trying to get to a team and contribute. But if I can't, then I can't wait to get back to the Army and serve in the same manner that I have."<ref name="nbc">{{cite web|last=Alper|first=Josh|title=Eagles sign U.S. Army Ranger Alejandro Villanueva|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/05/05/eagles-sign-army-ranger-alejandro-villanueva/|work=ProFootballTalk|publisher=NBC Sports|access-date=May 5, 2014|date=May 5, 2014}}</ref> During [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]], Villanueva gained {{convert|40|lb|kg}}, noting that he is eating a consistent diet, which contrasted with his military career insofar as while in the military, he often did not have time or inclination to eat, whereas with the Eagles, he was getting "plenty to eat".<ref>{{cite web|last1=Allibone |first1=Matt |title=Bulked up Villaneuva still adjusting to football |url=http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/bulked-villanueva-still-readjusting-football |website=CSNPhilly.com |publisher=Comcast SportsNet Philadelphia |access-date=August 9, 2014 |date=August 3, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140807051922/http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/bulked-villanueva-still-readjusting-football |archive-date=August 7, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Jasner|first1=Andy|title=Former Army Ranger Alejandro Villanueva making an impression|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/philadelphia-eagles/post/_/id/6774/former-army-ranger-making-an-impression|website=NFL Nation |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|access-date=August 9, 2014|date=August 4, 2014}}</ref> It was announced on August 23 that he was one of 14 players cut from the team.<ref>{{cite web | last=Santoliquito | first=Joseph | title=Eagles Cut Alejandro Villanueva | website=CBS News - Philadelphia | date=2014-08-23 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/eagles-cut-alejandro-villanueva/ | access-date=2026-03-04}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On August 21, 2014, during a pre-season game against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Villanueva was spotted by Steelers' head coach [[Mike Tomlin]], who was impressed with his size and athleticism. Eight days after he was waived by the Philadelphia Eagles, the Pittsburgh Steelers signed him to their practice squad on August 31, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://triblive.com/sports/joestarkey/6714049-74/villanueva-army-steelers| title=Starkey: Army vet earns instant respect with Steelers| access-date=February 1, 2017| website=triblive.com| author=Joe Starkey| date=September 3, 2014}}</ref> Upon joining his new team, he was immediately changed from a defensive end to an offensive tackle, as it was thought to better suit him. As a defensive end for the Eagles, Villanueva weighed 250 lb. Within a year of becoming an offensive tackle, he rose up to 340 lb.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pennlive.com/steelers/index.ssf/2015/10/steelers_alejandro_villanueva_discovery.html |title=How the Steelers discovered Alejandro Villanueva |access-date=October 2, 2015}}</ref>
Throughout the [[2014 Pittsburgh Steelers season|2014 season]], Villanueva was kept on the practice squad to learn the position, put on more weight, and develop his abilities.

====2015====
[[File:Alejandro Villanueva (American football).JPG|thumb|Villanueva with the Steelers in 2015]]
On January 6, 2015, the Pittsburgh Steelers signed him to a two-year, $960,000 reserve/futures contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/pittsburgh-steelers/alejandro-villanueva-14408/ |title=Sportrac.com:Alejandro Villanueva contract |access-date=October 18, 2016 |website=Sportrac.com}}</ref> He was able to get reps in training camp and preseason as the second-team swing tackle, after [[Mike Adams (offensive tackle)|Mike Adams]] suffered an injury. With Adams unable to recover before the regular season, Villanueva was slated as the Steelers' swing tackle to begin the 2015 season. He made his debut during the 2015 season opener against the [[2015 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]], playing five snaps as an extra tackle on goal-line plays.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.steelersdepot.com/2015/09/todd-haley-finds-new-tackle-eligible-in-alejandro-villanueva/| title=Todd Haley finds new tackle eligible in Alejandro Villanueva| date=September 14, 2015|access-date=September 15, 2015}}</ref> He also appeared on special teams and played a few plays at tight end during this period.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/from-army-ranger-to-steelers-tackle-villanueva-excels-at-protection/amp/ |title=From Army Ranger to Steelers left tackle, Villanueva excels at prptections |access-date=November 29, 2016| website=CBSsports.com| author=Ryan Wilson| date=November 11, 2015}}</ref>

On October 18, 2015, Villanueva received his first opportunity at left tackle against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] after starting left tackle [[Kelvin Beachum]] left the game with a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL]].

The following week, Villanueva received his first career start at offensive tackle since his sophomore year at Army in 2008 and was tasked with blocking [[Kansas City Chiefs]] Pro-Bowl defensive end, [[Tamba Hali]]. He allowed a strip sack in the fourth quarter, which aided the Chiefs in defeating the Steelers. With Beachum out for the remainder of the season, Villanueva continued to play left tackle and started the last 12 games of the Steelers' season, including two playoffs games. In his first season as a starter, he was ranked the 48th best offensive tackle by [[Pro Football Focus]] with an overall grade of 47.5.<ref name="playoff">{{cite web|url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/pro-how-pittsburghs-o-line-is-driving-the-steelers-playoff-push/| title=Steeler's Online is driving playoff push| access-date=January 29, 2017| website=profootballfocus.com| date=January 16, 2017}}</ref> He surrendered 39 pressures on 459 pass blocking snaps and ranked as the 11th-worst offensive tackle in pass blocking efficiency with a grade of 93.2 by PFF.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/pro-offseason-to-do-list-for-the-pittsburgh-steelers/ |title=Offseason to do list to the Pittsburgh Steelers |access-date=February 1, 2017 |website=profootballfocus.com|date=January 27, 2016 }}</ref>

====2016====
Villanueva was named the starting left tackle position to begin the [[2016 Pittsburgh Steelers season|2016 season]] after Kelvin Beachum left via free agency and after outperforming [[Ryan Harris (American football)|Ryan Harris]] in training camp.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alejandrovillanueva/2550130/profile |title=NFL Player Profile:Alejandro Villanueva |access-date=October 18, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Villanueva struggled early on in the season and surrendered five sacks in the first six games of the season. His run blocking and pass protection greatly improved after Week 7 and he only allowed one sack in the last ten games, helping the Pittsburgh Steelers reach the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/steelers-2016-2017-preview-playoffs-afc-championship-news-updates-roster-depth-chart-salary-cap-tickets-new-england-patriots-how-to-watch/2017/1/20/14314866/alejandro-villanuevas-growth-key-to-steelers-offensive-line-dominance-patriots-afc-championship| title=Alejandro Villanueva's growth key to Steeler's offensive line dominance| access-date=January 29, 2017| website=behindthesteelcurtain.com| date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> He finished the season ranking as the 23rd best offensive tackle in the league after receiving an 82.4 overall grade from [[Pro Football Focus]]. Including the three playoff games, Villanueva allowed 46 pressures and was penalized eight times in 19 starts with 26 of those pressures and five penalties coming in the first six regular season games. From Week 11 to the [[AFC Championship]], he performed well enough to rank as the best offensive tackle in that span.<ref name="playoff"/>

====2017====
On July 27, 2017, Villanueva signed a four-year, $24 million contract extension with the Steelers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers sign Alejandro Villanueva to 4-year, $24M deal|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-sign-alejandro-villanueva-to-4-year-24m-deal-0ap3000000822585|author=Rosenthal, Gregg|website=NFL.com|date=July 27, 2017}}</ref> Villanueva was credited with creating an [[audible (American football)|audible]] that included the phrase "[[Dilly Dilly]]" from a [[Bud Light]] television commercial, that quarterback [[Ben Roethlisberger]] later used in a live game.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/blog/pittsburgh-steelers/post/_/id/26059/steelers-take-titans-to-pit-of-misery-with-dilly-dilly-call Steelers take Titans to pit of misery with 'Dilly Dilly' call]. ''ESPN.com''. Retrieved November 17, 2017.</ref> On December 19, 2017, Villanueva was named to his first Pro Bowl along with fellow Steeler offensive linemen [[David DeCastro]] and [[Maurkice Pouncey]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NFL announces 2018 Pro Bowl rosters|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/updated-player-rosters-for-2018-pro-bowl-in-orlando-0ap3000000895772|website=NFL.com|date=December 19, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref> He became the first service academy graduate to play in the Pro Bowl since [[Roger Staubach]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite web| title=West Point grad, Steeler Alejandro Villanueva named Pro Bowl starter| url=https://www.armytimes.com/off-duty/military-sports/2017/12/20/west-point-grad-steeler-alejandro-villanueva-named-pro-bowl-starter/| access-date=January 22, 2018| website=ArmyTimes.com| author=Staff| date=December 20, 2017}}</ref> Villanueva started all 16 games in {{NFL Year|2017}} received an overall grade of 74.3 from [[Pro Football Focus]]. His grade ranked him 24th among all offensive tackles in the NFL.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Alejandro Villanueva| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/alejandro-villanueva/9091| access-date=January 22, 2018| website=ProFootballFocus.com}}</ref>

=====National anthem controversy=====

On September 24, 2017, prior to a game against the [[Chicago Bears]] at [[Soldier Field]], the Steelers did not take the field for the [[national anthem]] in order to avoid getting caught up in the controversy related to players kneeling or displaying other signs of racial [[U.S. national anthem protests (2016–present)|protest around the NFL]] started by [[Colin Kaepernick]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/08/23/sports/football/nfl-protest-colin-kaepernick.html|title=Kaepernick's Protest Cascades Into Protests Over His Job Situation|last=Belson|first=Ken|date=August 23, 2017|work=The New York Times|access-date=May 18, 2019|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Villanueva was the lone member of the Steelers to appear publicly for the [[national anthem]], standing in front of the entrance tunnel for the performance while the rest of the team remained in the tunnel. Head coach Mike Tomlin stated a wish to simply play the game and not allow for any show of support one way or the other on the issue.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers don't participate in national anthem, with exception of ex-Ranger Alejandro Villanueva|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2017/09/24/pittsburgh-steelers-national-anthem-mike-tomlin/697847001/|website=USA ====2018====
[[File:Myles Garrett (49093702366).jpg|thumb|Villanueva in a game against the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 2019]]
On November 25, 2018, Villanueva caught his first career touchdown pass on a fake field goal from Chris Boswell at the end of the first half in a game against the [[Denver Broncos]].
He received an overall grade of 78.1 from [[Pro Football Focus]] in 2018, which ranked as the 12th highest grade among all qualifying offensive tackles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/alejandro-villanueva/9091 |title=Pro Football Focus: Alejandro Villanueva |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=profootballfocus.com |access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>

==== 2020 ====
On September 28, 2020, Villanueva taped Sergeant First Class [[Alwyn Cashe]]'s name on the back of his helmet, covering the name of [[Shooting of Antwon Rose Jr.|Antwon Rose Jr]], who was killed by an East Pittsburgh police officer in June 2018 after being involved in a drive-by shooting.<ref name="triblive.com">{{Cite web|title=Who is Alwyn Cashe and why did Alejandro Villanueva choose to honor him? {{!}} TribLIVE.com|url=https://triblive.com/sports/steelers/who-is-alwyn-cashe-and-why-did-alejandro-villanueva-choose-to-honor-him/|access-date=2020-09-30|website=triblive.com|date=September 16, 2020}}</ref> Cashe was a US Army non-commissioned officer posthumously awarded the [[Silver Star]] ( Later upgraded to the Congressional Medal Of Honor) in 2005 for actions he took in [[Iraq War|Operation Iraqi Freedom]] to rescue soldiers from a burning vehicle, during which time he sustained burns over 75% of his body and ultimately succumbed to his injuries. The Steelers team had previously decided to honor Rose.<ref name="triblive.com"/> Villanueva stated his actions were intended to support the campaign to upgrade Cashe's award for valor from the Silver Star to the [[Medal of Honor]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Pryor | first=Brooke | title=Al Villanueva's helmet change catches Pittsburgh Steelers teammates by surprise | website=ESPN.com | date=2020-09-16 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29898200/al-villanueva-changes-name-helmet-dead-black-soldier-surprising-pittsburgh-steelers-teammates | access-date=2026-04-14}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On May 4, 2021, Villanueva signed a two-year, $14 million contract with the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-05-04|title=Ravens agree to deal with veteran offensive tackle Alejandro Villanueva|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-agree-to-deal-with-veteran-offensive-tackle-alejandro-villanueva|access-date=2021-05-05|website=Baltimore Ravens|language=en-US}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On March 9, 2022, Villanueva announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/alejandro-villanueva-retires-from-nfl-ravens-steelers-army|work=BaltimoreRavens.com|title=Ravens Place Alejandro Villanueva on Reserve/Retired List|date=March 9, 2022|accessdate=March 9, 2022|first=Clifton|last=Brown}}</ref>

After graduating from the United States Military Academy, Villanueva was commissioned into the United States Army on May 22, 2010, as a [[second lieutenant]] in the [[Infantry]].<ref name="Eagles/army">{{cite web|title=Eagles sign U.S. Army Ranger Villanueva|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Sign-US-Army-Ranger-Villanueva/cc530a5f-5c16-47b5-a546-5a8740dfd6a9|work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|publisher=Philadelphia Eagles|access-date=May 5, 2014|date=May 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140506005236/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Sign-US-Army-Ranger-Villanueva/cc530a5f-5c16-47b5-a546-5a8740dfd6a9|archive-date=May 6, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Directly after being commissioned he attended various military schools, including the [[United States Army Infantry School|Infantry]], [[United States Army Airborne School|Airborne]], and [[Ranger School]]s; all located at [[Fort Benning]], Georgia. After completing the three courses, he was assigned to the [[10th Mountain Division]] at [[Fort Drum]], New York. It was with the 10th Mountain Division he deployed for the first time for 12 months to [[Afghanistan]] in support of [[Operation Enduring Freedom - Afghanistan]] as a rifle platoon leader.<ref name="Eagles/army" /> As a result of his actions during this deployment he was awarded a [[Bronze Star Medal]] with [["V" device]] for rescuing wounded soldiers while under enemy fire.<ref name="Eagles/army" /> When he returned from his deployment, he was reassigned as a company [[executive officer]].<ref name="Eagles/army" />

Villanueva volunteered for the 75th Ranger Regiment's Ranger Orientation Program in 2013.<ref name="Eagles/army" /> He was assigned to the [[1st Ranger Battalion]]. His roles within the Battalion have included [[S3 (military)#Plans & Strategy (5)|plans officer]], [[platoon leader]], and company executive officer.<ref name="Eagles/army" />

He has deployed two more times to Afghanistan for a total of eight months between both deployments.<ref name="Eagles/army" /> In 2015, Villanueva left the army when downsizing efforts meant he would have to wait 18 months for a command position that would last less than 12 months.<ref name="moaa.org">{{cite web|title=From being an Army Ranger to an NFL star|url=https://www.moaa.org/content/publications-and-media/news-articles/2019-news-articles/soldier-to-steeler-nfl-star-shares-insight-to-military-service/|website=MOAA.org|access-date=September 17, 2020|date=September 27, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Villanueva has spoken publicly about the importance of his [[Catholicism|Catholic]] faith in his life and work.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.pittsburghcatholic.org/News/Faith-warrior--Steelers-lineman-builds-ties-to-God-| title=Faith warrior: Steeler's lineman builds ties to God| access-date=February 1, 2017| website=Pittsburghcatholic.org| author=John Frank| date=February 22, 2016| archive-date=February 3, 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203025414/http://www.pittsburghcatholic.org/News/Faith-warrior--Steelers-lineman-builds-ties-to-God-| url-status=dead}}</ref> In November 2013, he married Madelyn Muldoon in a small ceremony in her parents' backyard. He met her through her brother, Joe Muldoon, with whom he played football at Army, and the two began dating in the spring of 2012.<ref name="path"/> On May 9, 2015, Alejandro and Madelyn had a larger ceremony at the Jesus the Divine Word Catholic Church in [[Huntingtown, Maryland]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.weddingwire.com/weddings/3541338/wedding_new_website#!/website/2415627| title=Alejandro & Madelyn: Happily Ever After| access-date=February 1, 2017| website=weddingwire.com| archive-date=September 25, 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925132125/https://www.weddingwire.com/weddings/3541338/wedding_new_website#!/website/2415627| url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the fall of 2015, Villanueva enrolled in [[Carnegie Mellon University|Carnegie Mellon University's]] [[Tepper School of Business]] to earn a [[Master of Business Administration]] (MBA) degree. After studying part-time for four years, one more than is typical for a student in Tepper's MBA program, Villanueva received his degree in 2019.<ref name="mba">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=June 7, 2019 |title=Alejandro Villanueva earns MBA from Carnegie Mellon |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/06/07/alejandro-villanueva-earns-mba-from-carnegie-mellon/ |access-date=October 29, 2019 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Universal}}</ref>

'''Albert Wilson II''' (born July 12, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and [[Miami Dolphins]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia State Panthers football|Georgia State Panthers]]. He holds several Georgia State records, including most touchdown receptions, longest pass play, and longest punt return.<ref name="A">{{Cite web |title=#2 Albert Wilson |url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=204967197 |access-date=September 7, 2014 |website=Georgia State Panthers Athletics |archive-date=August 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827072244/http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=204967197 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 GSU Football Guide |url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/fls/12700/stats/2017Football/2017GSUFBMG.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=12700 |access-date=November 3, 2017 |website=Georgia State Panthers Athletics |archive-date=March 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324003017/http://www.georgiastatesports.com/fls/12700/stats/2017Football/2017GSUFBMG.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=12700 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Early life==
Wilson was born in [[Fort Pierce, Florida]] to an African-American father and Samoan mother.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Charlie |date=November 27, 2013 |title=From Escape Routes to Pass Routes -- Part 2 |url=https://georgiastatesports.com/news/2013/11/27/209322823.aspx |access-date=October 18, 2020 |publisher=Georgia State University |archive-date=October 19, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019084322/https://georgiastatesports.com/news/2013/11/27/209322823.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> Because his parents served time in prison, Wilson grew up in foster care. In tenth grade, he was adopted by Brian and Rose Bailey of [[Port St. Lucie, Florida]]. After his parents were released from prison, Wilson moved in with a cousin who lived in Port St. Lucie so that he could stay in his high school.<ref name="blind side">{{Cite web |last=Covitz |first=Randy |date=September 20, 2014 |title=Chiefs wide receiver Albert Wilson's story reads like a sequel to 'The Blind Side' |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article2185670.html |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=The Kansas City Star |archive-date=November 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123120224/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article2185670.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Wilson played quarterback for the [[Port St. Lucie High School]] Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Lindsay |date=August 9, 2018 |title=Dolphins receivers Albert Wilson, Kenny Stills kneel in protest during national anthem |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2018/08/09/nfl-players-protest-kneel-national-anthem-kenny-stills-albert-wilson/953220002/ |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=USA TODAY |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006200323/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2018/08/09/nfl-players-protest-kneel-national-anthem-kenny-stills-albert-wilson/953220002/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was named [[Treasure Coast Newspapers|Scripps Treasure Coast Newspapers]] All-Area Offensive Player of the Year in 2010 as a senior. He recorded 2,631 all-purpose yards, and 22 touchdowns his senior year. His totals were 1,029 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns, 824 rushing yards, 11 rushing touchdowns, 81 receiving yards, 132 interception return yards and 565 return yards.<ref name="A" /> Wilson also ran track for Port St. Lucie High School and competed in the 100m, 200m, 100 high hurdles where he placed in states.{{Citation needed|date=April 2018}}

==College career==
Wilson played for the [[Georgia State Panthers football|Georgia State Panthers]] from 2010 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Wilson College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/albert-wilson-1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006195249/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/albert-wilson-1.html |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was the first Georgia State player to be invited to the [[NFL Combine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2014 |title=Wilson Performs Well at NFL Combine |url=https://georgiastatesports.com/sports/2014/2/24/209416173.aspx |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=Georgia State University |language=en |archive-date=March 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230305204247/https://georgiastatesports.com/sports/2014/2/24/209416173.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> He had a career total of 6,235 all-purpose yards, which ranked among the top thirty in [[NCAA]] history. Wilson became the Panthers' all-time leading scorer with 26 touchdowns. He also became the leading receiver in Georgia State history after recording 175 receptions for 3,190 yards and 23 touchdowns. He set school records in kickoff returns with 95 and kickoff return yards with 2,338 and returned two kickoffs for touchdowns. Wilson also held the records for career punt returns with 41 and yards with 376. He had the longest reception (93 yards), longest run (80), longest kickoff return (100) and longest punt return (62) in school history. He earned Honorable Mention [[All-American]] honors from [[SI.com]] in 2013. Wilson also garnered First-team All-[[Sun Belt Conference|Sun Belt]] accolades in 2013. He was named First-team All-[[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] as a kick returner and Third-team All-CAA as a wide receiver in 2012. He was also CAA Special Teams Co-Player of the Year in 2012.<ref name="A" />

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On May 11, 2014, the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] signed Wilson as an [[undrafted free agent]] after he went unselected in the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thorman |first=Chris |date=May 10, 2014 |title=Tracking the 2014 Kansas City Chiefs undrafted free agent signings |url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2014/5/10/5703596/kc-chiefs-undrafted-free-agent-signings-2014-college-free-agents-udfas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230305204507/https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2014/5/10/5703596/kc-chiefs-undrafted-free-agent-signings-2014-college-free-agents-udfas |archive-date=March 5, 2023 |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=Arrowhead Pride|publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref> The Chiefs signed him to a three-year, [[United states dollar|$]]1.54 million contract with a [[signing bonus]] of $10,000.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Albert Wilson contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/albert-wilson-14949/ |access-date=December 31, 2017 |website=Spotrac.com |archive-date=January 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102021158/http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/albert-wilson-14949/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

He made his NFL debut on September 7, 2014, against the [[2014 Tennessee Titans|Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Wilson |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/albertwilson/2550272/gamelogs |access-date=September 7, 2014 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=September 8, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140908065103/http://www.nfl.com/player/albertwilson/2550272/gamelogs |url-status=live }}</ref> He recorded his first professional reception in the following game against the [[2014 San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at San Diego Chargers – October 19th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410190sdg.htm |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006195245/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410190sdg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, in his rookie season, he finished with 16 receptions for 260 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Wilson 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006194959/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Wilson finished the 2015 regular-season as the Chiefs' third-leading receiver with 35 receptions for 451 yards and 2 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Kansas City Chiefs Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2015.htm |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 22, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222214035/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2015.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The Chiefs finished the regular season with an 11–5 record and qualified for the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs]]. The Chiefs were eliminated by the [[2015 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]] in the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 27, Kansas City Chiefs 20|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2015/gamelog/ |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006194805/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2015/gamelog/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Wilson finished the playoffs with 7 receptions for 66 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Wilson Playoffs Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/post/ |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006194749/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/post/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Wilson finished the 2016 regular-season with 31 receptions for 279 yards for two touchdowns and one rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Wilson 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006195241/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Chiefs finished the regular season with a 12–4 record and qualified for the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Kansas City Chiefs Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2016.htm |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181005180647/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2016.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 18, Kansas City Chiefs 16|Divisional Round]] against the [[2016 Pittsburgh Steelers|Pittsburgh Steelers]], he had two receptions for three yards and a touchdown in the 18–16 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Pittsburgh Steelers at Kansas City Chiefs – January 15th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701150kan.htm |access-date=December 5, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106173254/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701150kan.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
[[File:Albert Wilson (American football).jpg|thumb|Wilson with the Chiefs in 2017]]
On March 9, 2017, the Chiefs signed Wilson to a one-year, $1.79 million extension.<ref name="spotrac" /> In the 2017 season, Wilson finished with 42 receptions for 554 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Albert Wilson 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=October 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006195332/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WilsAl02/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

|archive-date=April 19, 2018 |access-date=March 16, 2018 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> In Week 3 of the 2018 season, Wilson recorded two receptions for 74 yards and threw a 52-yard touchdown pass He played [[college football]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|BYU Cougars]] from 2010 to 2014. ==Professional career== ===Arizona Cardinals=== Fua was signed by the Arizona Cardinals as an undrafted free agent on May 2, 2015.{{cite web|title=Cardinals Bring In 14 Undrafted Rookies|url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Bring-In-14-Undrafted-Rookies/1b8a570e-0a35-41f5-92f9-a430dca19220|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170731234444/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Bring-In-14-Undrafted-Rookies/1b8a570e-0a35-41f5-92f9-a430dca19220|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 31, 2017|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=May 5, 2015|accessdate=July 31, 2017}} On September 28, 2016, Fua was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury.{{cite web|title=Cardinals Add Aaron Brewer To Snap|url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Add-Aaron-Brewer-To-Snap/8b2ad98e-c8c6-4269-872d-43ff281e081e|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|accessdate=September 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160929135258/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Add-Aaron-Brewer-To-Snap/8b2ad98e-c8c6-4269-872d-43ff281e081e|archive-date=September 29, 2016|url-status=dead}} On July 31, 2017, Fua was waived/injured by the Cardinals and placed on injured reserve.{{cite web|title=Cardinals add another cornerback|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/07/31/cardinals-add-another-cornerback/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=July 31, 2017}} He was released on September 18, 2017. ==Personal life== Alani Fua is of [[Tongan American|Tongan descent]], the son of George and Helen Fua. ===New Orleans Saints===
Darby signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]]. On August 4, 2016, Darby was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints' Alden Darby: Placed on IR|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/saints-alden-darby-placed-on-ir/}}</ref> On August 7, 2016, he was released by the Saints with an injury settlement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alden Darby: Reaches injury settlement with Saints|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alden-darby-reaches-injury-settlement-with-saints/}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On August 17, 2016, Darby signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alden Darby: Signs with Indianapolis|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alden-darby-signs-with-indianapolis/}}</ref> On August 28, 2016, Darby was waived by the Colts,<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Begin Roster Cuts, Waive 10 Players, Sign Stevan Ridley|url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Begin-Roster-Cuts-Waive-10-Players-Sign-Stevan-Ridley/905a93ed-ebe2-4070-841d-ed21537829ac|last=Bowen|first=Kevin|website=Colts.com|access-date=2016-08-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160831031818/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Begin-Roster-Cuts-Waive-10-Players-Sign-Stevan-Ridley/905a93ed-ebe2-4070-841d-ed21537829ac|archive-date=2016-08-31|url-status=dead}}</ref> but was re-signed two days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indianapolis Colts sign S-Alden Darby|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2016/08/30/indianapolis-colts-sign-s-alden-darby-2/|website=Colts.com|access-date=August 31, 2016|archive-date=August 31, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160831133036/http://blogs.colts.com/2016/08/30/indianapolis-colts-sign-s-alden-darby-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On September 3, 2016, he was waived by the Colts as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Make Final Cuts, Assemble 53-Man Roster|url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Make-Final-Cuts-Assemble-53-Man-Roster/37b970e3-453c-4747-a62d-5e74c9161c02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814143331/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Make-Final-Cuts-Assemble-53-Man-Roster/37b970e3-453c-4747-a62d-5e74c9161c02|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2017|last=Bowen|first=Kevin|website=Colts.com|date=September 3, 2016}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On July 16, 2017, Darby was signed to the practice roster of the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2017/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 12, 2022}}</ref> He played in eight regular season games with the Argonauts in [[2017 Toronto Argonauts season|2017]] where he had 18 defensive tackles and one interception that he returned 75 yards for his first career touchdown. He was on the injured list when the team won the [[105th Grey Cup]]. He re-signed with the Argonauts on January 25, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Argos add former Steeler Martavis Bryant and re-sign Alden Darby |url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2021/01/25/argos-add-former-steeler-martavis-bryant-re-sign-alden-darby/ |website=Argonauts.ca |date=January 25, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2021}}</ref>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (first stint)===
On July 19, 2021, Darby was traded to the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] in exchange for [[offensive lineman]] [[Terry Poole (American football)|Terry Poole]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Blue Bombers acquire defensive back Alden Darby from Argonauts |url=https://www.bluebombers.com/2021/07/19/blue-bombers-acquire-defensive-back-alden-darby-argonauts/ |publisher=[[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] |date=July 19, 2021}}</ref> He played in 11 regular season games where he had 34 defensive tackles and was named a CFL West All-Star. He finished the season as a [[Grey Cup]] champion as the Blue Bombers won the [[108th Grey Cup]]. He became a free agent upon the expiry of his contract on February 8, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2022/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 8, 2022}}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
Darby signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] as a free agent on February 10, 2022, after initially verbally agreeing to join the [[Ottawa Redblacks]].<ref>{{cite news |title=NFL FOR MICAH? Redblacks sign Cunningham and Washington, Awe hoping for NFL opportunity |url=https://ottawasun.com/sports/football/cfl/ottawa-redblacks/nfl-for-micah-redblacks-sign-cunningham-and-washington-awe-hoping-for-nfl-opportunity |publisher=[[Ottawa Sun]] |date=February 10, 2022}}</ref> He played in ten games where he recorded 23 tackles, one sack, and one interception.<ref name=HAMWPG>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2022/10/04/bombers-acquire-alden-darby-jr-in-trade-w-ticats/ |title=Bombers acquire Alden Darby Jr. in trade w/ Ticats |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=October 4, 2022}}</ref>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (second stint)===
On October 4, 2022, the day before the trade deadline, Darby was traded to the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] in exchange for [[Cedric Wilcots]].<ref name=HAMWPG/> He played in two regular season games where he recorded six defensive tackles.<ref name=2023Guide>{{cite web|url=https://static.cfl.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023-CFL-Guide-PDF-for-site.pdf |title=2023 CFL Guide |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=May 5, 2024}}</ref> He also played in the West Final playoff and the [[109th Grey Cup]] game, where he recorded three defensive tackles, but the Blue Bombers lost to the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref name=2023Guide/>

In [[2023 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|2023]], Darby played in 11 regular season games, starting in six, where he recorded 20 defensive tackles and three special teams tackles. He sustained an injury mid-season as was placed on the six-game injured list on September 2, 2023, and did not play again that season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://3downnation.com/2023/09/02/bombers-place-db-alden-darby-on-six-game-injured-list-ahead-of-rivalry-clash-with-riders/ |title=Bombers place DB Alden Darby on six-game injured list ahead of rivalry clash with Riders |publisher=3DownNation |date=September 2, 2023}}</ref> He became a [[free agent]] upon the expiry of his contract on February 13, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/fa24/ |title=Official 2024 Free Agent Tracker |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=May 22, 2024}}</ref>

On June 6, 2024, Darby announced his retirement via [[X (Twitter)]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=x.com |url=https://x.com/Pic6Darb/status/1798868207975137663 |access-date=2024-06-07 |website=X (formerly Twitter)}}</ref>

'''Alan Stephen Harper''' (born September 6, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] for one season with the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]] and was selected by the Jets in the fourth round of the [[2002 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Harper played [[high school football]] at [[Fontana High School]] in [[Fontana, California]], and graduated in 1997. He earned first-team All-[[Citrus Belt League]] and All-[[Inland Valley League|Inland Valley]] honors his senior year in 1996. He recorded 63 unassisted tackles, 24 assisted tackles, eight sacks and three pass deflections while the team went 11–1–1 in 1996. Harper attended [[A. B. Miller High School]] in Fontana his sophomore and junior years, garnering All-[[San Andreas League]] accolades twice.<ref name="B">{{Cite web |title=ALAN HARPER |url=http://www.gobulldogs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/alan_harper_4039.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219173238/http://www.gobulldogs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/alan_harper_4039.html |archive-date=February 19, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=gobulldogs.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Harper played for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]] from 1998 to 2001. He sat out the 1997 season while fulfilling academic requirements. He earned first-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] honors in 1999, 2000 and 2001. Harper was Fresno State's nominee for WAC Defensive Player of the Year in 1999 and won the award in 2001. He was also named a second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] by [[The Sporting News]] his senior season in 2001.<ref name="B" />

==Professional career==
Harper was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the fourth round with the 121st pick in the [[2002 NFL draft]] and signed with the team on July 24, 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2002/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="A" /><ref name="C">{{Cite web |title=Alan Harper |url=http://sportsforecaster.com/nfl/player/5053/trans |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219174706/http://sportsforecaster.com/nfl/player/5053/trans |archive-date=February 19, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=sportsforecaster.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ALAN HARPER |url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/alan-harper-player-transactions |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219173855/http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/alan-harper-player-transactions |archive-date=February 19, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |work=foxsports.com}}</ref> He was released by the Jets on October 15, 2003, and signed to the team's practice squad on October 16, 2003.<ref name="C" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2003 |title=TRANSACTIONS |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/10/17/sports/transactions-731846.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219175934/http://www.nytimes.com/2003/10/17/sports/transactions-731846.html |archive-date=February 19, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |work=nytimes.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 17, 2003.<ref name="D">{{Cite web |title=Alan Harper |url=http://www.kffl.com/player/5799/nfl/news |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219174234/http://www.kffl.com/player/5799/nfl/news |archive-date=February 19, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=kffl.com}}</ref> Harper was allocated to [[NFL Europe]] on February 9, 2004, where he played for the [[Scottish Claymores]].<ref name="D" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alan Harper |url=http://www.justsportsstats.com/footballstatsindex.php?player_id=harpeala001 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=StatsCrew.com}}</ref> He was named to the All-NFL Europe Team for his play during the [[2004 NFL Europe season|2004 season]].<ref name="D" /> He was released by the Jets on September 5 and signed to the team's practice squad on September 6, 2004. Harper was promoted to the active roster on September 27, 2004.<ref name="C" /><ref name="D" /> He played in eleven games for the Jets during the [[2004 NFL season|2004 season]].<ref name="A">{{Cite web |title=ALAN HARPER |url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/harp00080.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160215085444/http://www.profootballarchives.com/harp00080.html |archive-date=February 15, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=profootballarchives.com}}</ref> He was released by the Jets on August 31, 2005.<ref name="D" />

Harper was signed by the [[San Jose SaberCats]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) on December 19, 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historical Team Transactions |url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=25 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219040358/http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=25 |archive-date=February 19, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=arenafan.com}}</ref> He played for the team from 2006 to 2008.<ref name="E">{{Cite web |title=Alan Harper |url=http://www.arenafan.com/players/Alan_Harper-5159/ |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=arenafan.com}}</ref>

Harper signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on February 11, 2009.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ticats.ca/2009/02/11/tiger-cats-sign-two-defensive-linemen/ | title=TIGER-CATS SIGN TWO DEFENSIVE LINEMEN | publisher=[[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] | date=February 11, 2009 | accessdate=12 April 2026}}</ref> He was released during final roster cuts on June 25, 2009.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2009/06/25/across-the-cfl-cut-down-day-2009/ | title=ACROSS THE CFL: CUT DOWN DAY 2009 | publisher=[[CFL.ca]] | date=June 25, 2009 | accessdate=12 April 2026}}</ref> He was signed to the practice roster of the CFL's [[BC Lions]] on November 18, 2009.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919003305/http://bclions.com/page/2009-transactions | title=2009 Transactions | publisher=[[BC Lions]] | accessdate=12 April 2026}}</ref>

Harper signed with the [[Arizona Rattlers]] of the AFL on June 30, 2010, and played for the team during the [[2010 Arena Football League season|2010 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historical Team Transactions |url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314200853/http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=21 |archive-date=March 14, 2015 |access-date=February 19, 2016 |publisher=arenafan.com}}</ref><ref name="E" />

'''Alex Balducci''' (born March 1, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon Ducks]], and signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=Barrows |first=Matt |title=49ers notes: Next man up on O-line may be rookie Balducci |newspaper=[[Sacramento Bee]] |date=December 13, 2016 |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nfl/san-francisco-49ers/article120683083.html |access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Balducci played [[nose tackle]] for [[Oregon Ducks football|Ducks]] at the [[University of Oregon]] from 2012 to 2015. As a redshirt freshman in 2012, he sat out the first ten games but played the last four games after many injuries to the defensive line. As a freshman, he played under his future 49ers head coach [[Chip Kelly]].<ref name="Oregon">{{cite web|url=http://www.goducks.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4265| title=Oregon Ducks football: Alex Balducci| access-date=December 14, 2015| website=goducks.com}}</ref> On November 10, 2012, he made his collegiate debut in a 19–17 victory over [[2012 California Golden Bears football team|California]]. He got his first collegiate start the following week against [[2012 Stanford Cardinal football team|Stanford]]. On November 24, 2012, he made his first career tackle during a 48–24 victory over No. 16 [[2012 Oregon State Beavers football team|Oregon State]]. He finished his freshman season with one tackle in four games.

The following year, he played in 10 games during his sophomore season and made 18 combined tackles. As a junior, he played in ten games, made 18 total tackles, three tackles for a loss, and a sack. In 2015, Balducci played in all 13 games and had a career-high 40 combined tackles, 7.5 tackles for a loss, and 3.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Balducci College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alex-balducci-1.html |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On May 6, 2016, the [[San Francisco 49ers]] signed Balducci to a three-year, $1.35 million undrafted free agent contract with $57,500 guaranteed and a signing bonus of $12,500.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2016/5/30/11812870/49ers-roster-breakdowns-90-in-90-ol-alex-balducci| title=49er's roster breakdown: 90 in 90 OL Alex Balducci| access-date=December 14, 2016| website=ninersnation.com}}</ref> This reunited him with his former head coach at [[University of Oregon|Oregon]] and former 49ers' head coach Chip Kelly. Throughout mini-camps, Kelly and the 49ers' coaching staff worked with Balducci in an attempt to convert him into an offensive lineman. On September 3, 2016, he was waived by the 49ers as a part of their final roster cuts. The next day, he was signed to their practice squad. On December 12, 2016, the 49ers promoted Balducci to the active roster after a season-ending injury to [[Daniel Kilgore (American football)|Daniel Kilgore]] and an injury to [[Fahn Cooper]].<ref name="scout"/>

On December 24, 2016, he made his professional regular season debut in the 49ers' 22–21 victory over the [[2016 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]]. The following week, he played in the 49ers' 25–23 loss to the [[2016 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]]. He finished his rookie season appearing in two games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alexbalducci/2556465/profile| title=NFL Player Profile: Alex Balducci| access-date=January 4, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On May 2, 2017, Balducci was waived by the 49ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Several Roster Moves|url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Announce-Several-Roster-Moves/76eef6e9-d2d1-432c-b450-1ed362cf110f?sf75387211=1|website=49ers.com|date=May 2, 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171216153656/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Announce-Several-Roster-Moves/76eef6e9-d2d1-432c-b450-1ed362cf110f?sf75387211=1|archive-date = December 16, 2017}}</ref>

===New York Jets (first stint)===
On May 3, 2017, Balducci was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Acquire OL Alex Balducci Off Waivers|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Acquire-OL-Alex-Balducci-Off-Waivers/7fcc9abf-5ade-4f41-b0a8-0d627a15f847|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=May 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903204144/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Acquire-OL-Alex-Balducci-Off-Waivers/7fcc9abf-5ade-4f41-b0a8-0d627a15f847|archive-date=September 3, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Reduce to 53 with 23 Player Moves|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Reduce-to-53-with-23-Player-Moves/cc228adf-8efd-4ebf-9482-5cd637b6b638|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171207085306/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Reduce-to-53-with-23-Player-Moves/cc228adf-8efd-4ebf-9482-5cd637b6b638|archive-date=December 7, 2017}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On September 11, 2017, Balducci was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=9/11: Redskins Make Roster Moves|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/911-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/822342bb-4dfd-4968-b517-c1cd9e034e4e|website=Redskins.com|date=September 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302223400/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/911-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/822342bb-4dfd-4968-b517-c1cd9e034e4e|archive-date=March 2, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Redskins on January 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign 11 Players To Reserve/Future Contracts|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-11-Players-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/c6f20f93-73d6-4275-9173-5e8d96ee85b0|website=Redskins.com|date=January 1, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103202113/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-11-Players-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/c6f20f93-73d6-4275-9173-5e8d96ee85b0|archive-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on August 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=8/1: Redskins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/8-1-redskins-make-roster-moves |website=Redskins.com |date=August 1, 2018 |access-date=August 1, 2018 |archive-date=August 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801190352/https://www.redskins.com/news/8-1-redskins-make-roster-moves |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New York Jets (second stint)===
On August 6, 2018, Balducci signed with the New York Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign OL Alex Balducci, Waive Austin Golson|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-ol-alex-balducci-waive-austin-golson|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 6, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Cut 18 Players on Their Way to 53-Player Active Roster|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-cut-18-players-on-their-way-to-53-player-active-roster|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref>

===Arizona Hotshots===
Balducci signed a contract with the [[Arizona Hotshots]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] (AAF) on March 25, 2019, while on the team's rights list. He was activated from the rights list on March 26. The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===Dallas Renegades===
Balducci was selected in the 5th round in phase two in the [[2020 XFL draft]] by the [[Dallas Renegades]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-2-offensive-line-draft-tracker |title=OFFENSIVE LINEMEN DRAFT TRACKER |website=XFL.com |date=October 15, 2019 |access-date=October 16, 2019 |archive-date=October 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016142541/https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-2-offensive-line-draft-tracker |url-status=dead }}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

'''Alex Anzalone''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|n|z|ə|ˈ|l|oʊ|n|i}} {{respell|an|zə|LOW|nee}}, born September 22, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]]. Anzalone was selected in the third round by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the [[2017 NFL draft]].

==College career==
Anzalone originally committed to [[Ohio State]] and [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]] but chose to play [[college football]] at [[Florida Gators football|University of Florida]] from 2013 to 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone – Football |url=https://floridagators.com/sports/football/roster/alex-anzalone/6164 |website=Florida Gators}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gatorcountry.com/florida-gators-football/2017-nfl-draft-alex-anzalone-drafted/ |title=2017 NFL Draft: Alex Anzalone drafted by Saints |date=April 28, 2017 |last=Carlton |first=Bailiegh |website=Gator Country |access-date=December 2, 2024}}</ref> 

During the four-year span, he missed 20 games due to injuries with his only full season being the 2014 season as the backup linebacker. He played ten games in 2013, two games in 2015, and seven games in 2016.<ref name="n787">{{cite web | last=Lieser | first=Jason | title=2017 NFL Draft: Florida Gators LB Alex Anzalone an option for Dolphins | website=Palm Beach Post | date=February 3, 2017 | url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/2017/02/03/2017-nfl-draft-florida-gators/7144423007/ | access-date=October 22, 2024}}</ref><ref name="h422">{{cite web | last=Solomon | first=Jon | title=Reintroducing five-star Alex Anzalone, Florida's tenacious defensive supernova | website=CBSSports.com | date=September 20, 2016 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/reintroducing-five-star-alex-anzalone-floridas-tenacoius-defensive-supernova/ | access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref><ref name="b247">{{cite web | last=Erickson | first=Joel | title=Florida's Alex Anzalone has the tools to fit NFL's new linebacker template if he can stay healthy | website=The Advocate | date=February 22, 2017 | url=https://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/saints/article_6655be9c-f925-11e6-9084-c30ce9594c8f.html | access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref><ref name="x552">{{cite web | last=Aschoff | first=Edward | title=Florida's Alex Anzalone is back and ready to show who he really is in 2016 | website=ESPN.com | date=August 24, 2016 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/119504/floridas-alex-anzalone-is-back-and-ready-to-show-who-he-really-is-in-2016 | access-date=October 22, 2024}}</ref> He forewent his final year of college eligibility to enter the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/florida-lb-alex-anzalone-leaving-early-for-nfl-draft |title=Florida LB Alex Anzalone leaving early for NFL draft |website=Fox Sports |date=January 4, 2017 |access-date=December 2, 2024}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
The [[New Orleans Saints]] selected Anzalone in the third round (76th overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 28, 2017 |title=New Orleans Saints pick LB Alex Anzalone in the third round of the 2017 NFL Draft |url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-pick-LB-Alex-Anzalone-in-the-third-round-of-the-2017-NFL-Draft/9bc2018b-54dc-4ce7-9600-0e8730119269 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> He was the tenth [[linebacker]] selected in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=May 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On June 2, 2017, the Saints signed Anzalone to a four-year, $3.46 million contract that included a [[signing bonus]] of $864,592.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Alex Anzalone contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-orleans-saints/alex-anzalone-21818/ |access-date=April 14, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Anzalone earned a starting outside linebacker job for the Saints as a rookie, starting all four games in which he played. In Week 4 against the Dolphins, he suffered a shoulder injury and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 4, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Erickson |first=Joel A. |date=October 4, 2017 |title=New Orleans Saints lose rookie linebacker Alex Anzalone to injured reserve |url=http://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/saints/article_2299b6d4-a94e-11e7-9461-8f43021e2a94.html |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=TheAdvocate.com}}</ref>

He played in all 16 games, starting seven, in the 2018 season. He finished with two sacks, 59 total tackles (45 solo), one interception, two passes defended, and three forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Anzalone was placed on injured reserve on September 16, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=September 16, 2019 |title=Saints place Alex Anzalone on injured reserve |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/saints-place-alex-anzalone-on-injured-reserve-2 |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> In the 2019 season, he appeared in two games and had one sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2020 season, he appeared in 16 games and started nine. He finished with 41 total tackles (22 solo).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
Anzalone signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] on March 24, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 24, 2021 |title=Lions sign LB Alex Anzalone and WR Damion Ratley |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-lb-alex-anzalone-and-wr-damion-ratley |access-date=March 24, 2021 |work=DetroitLions.com}}</ref> He entered the 2021 season as a starting linebacker. He started the first 14 games before suffering a shoulder injury in Week 15. He was placed on injured reserve on December 20.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 20, 2021 |title=Lions lose LB Alex Anzalone for the season with shoulder injury |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2021/12/20/detroit-lions-lose-alex-anzalone-season-shoulder-injury/8972907002/ |website=DetroitNews.com}}</ref> In the 2021 season, he appeared in and started 14 games. He finished with one sack, 78 total tackles (49 solo), one interception, and seven passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In March 2022, Anzalone re-signed with the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2022 |title=Lions re-sign LB Alex Anzalone, S Jalen Elliott, LB Shaun Dion Hamilton and S C.J. Moore |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-re-sign-lb-alex-anzalone-s-jalen-elliott-lb-shaun-dion-hamilton-and-s-c-j- |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he started in all 17 games. He finished with 1.5 sacks, 125 total tackles (77 solo), one interception, six passes defended, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2023, Anzalone signed a three-year, $18.75 million contract extension with the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 13, 2023 |title=Report: Alex Anzalone agrees to three-year, $18.75 million deal to return to Lions |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/03/13/alex-anzalone-agrees-to-three-year-18-75-million-deal-to-return-to-lions/amp/ |website=NBCSports.com |access-date=March 14, 2023 |archive-date=March 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314051621/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/03/13/alex-anzalone-agrees-to-three-year-18-75-million-deal-to-return-to-lions/amp/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the 2023 season, Anzalone finished with three sacks, 129 total tackles (85 solo), six passes defended, and one fumble recovery in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=October 22, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In his third season with the Lions, Anzalone was selected as a 2024 NFL Pro Bowl alternate.<ref name="a622">{{cite web | last=Maakaron | first=John | title=Five Lions selected for Pro Bowl Games, as NFL reveals Pro Bowlers, alternates | website=The Oakland Press | date=January 4, 2024 | url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/2024/01/03/five-lions-selected-for-pro-bowl-games-as-nfl-reveals-pro-bowlers-alternates/ | access-date=October 22, 2024}}</ref>

In the 2024 season Anzalone suffered a broken left forearm in the Week 11's 52-6 victory against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. Expected to miss 6-8 weeks due to the injury, he was placed on injured reserve on November 18 with hopes of returning in the post-season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/lions-put-alex-anzalone-ir-220348930.html |title=Lions put Alex Anzalone on IR, sign David Long to practice squad |date=November 18, 2024 |access-date=December 2, 2024 |website=Yahoo Sports}}</ref> Prior to the injury, Anzalone totaled 56 stops, including seven tackles for loss, and four pass deflections.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Anzalone 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AnzaAl00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2024-12-25 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was activated for the regular season finale on January 4, 2025.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 12, 2026, Anzalone signed a two-year, $17 million contract with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Sign LB Alex Anzalone on Two-Year Deal|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-lb-alex-anzalone-two-year-deal|author=Dix, Brianna|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 12, 2026}}</ref>

'''Aldrick Rosas''' {{Respell|al|DREEK row|SOS}}; (born December 30, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[placekicker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Southern Oregon Raiders football |Southern Oregon Raiders]]. Rosas was selected to the [[2019 Pro Bowl|Pro Bowl]] for the [[2018 NFL season|2018 season]] as a member of the [[New York Giants]].

== College career ==
Rosas who is of [[Mexican Americans|Mexican–American]] descent, played [[college football]] for the [[Southern Oregon Raiders football|Southern Oregon Raiders]] of the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics]] (NAIA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.souraiders.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2696|title=Aldrick Rosas - 2014|access-date=April 25, 2017|archive-date=April 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426061249/http://www.souraiders.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2696|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2014, he tore the ACL in his kicking leg making a [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackle]] in the [[NAIA Football National Championship|NAIA Championship Game]]. After missing the 2015 season, he decided to forego the remainder of college eligibility to pursue a career in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2017/09/the_story_of_aldrick_rosas_journey_from_small_oreg.html|title=The incredible story of Aldrick Rosas' journey from small Oregon school to Giants' kicker|first=Dan|last=Duggan|website=NJ.com|access-date=September 30, 2018|archive-date=September 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930231219/https://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2017/09/the_story_of_aldrick_rosas_journey_from_small_oreg.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
Following the conclusion of the [[2016 NFL draft]], Rosas signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 9, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Agree to Terms with 11 Undrafted Free time Agents|url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-11-undrafted-free-agents-17130755|website=TitansOnline.com|date=May 9, 2016|access-date=June 17, 2017|archive-date=September 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919132623/https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-11-undrafted-free-agents-17130755|url-status=live}}</ref> On September 2, Rosas was waived by the Titans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Down to 53 Players: A Position-by-Position Look|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/628127bc-7013-4906-a04d-bd1f9e8ce8fa|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=September 2, 2016|access-date=June 17, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807023144/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/628127bc-7013-4906-a04d-bd1f9e8ce8fa|archive-date=August 7, 2017}}</ref>

===New York Giants===

==== 2017 season ====
On January 19, 2017, Rosas signed a reserve/future contract with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://giantswire.usatoday.com/2017/01/19/new-york-giants-sign-kicker-aldrick-rosas-to-reservefutures-deal/|title=New York Giants sign kicker Aldrick Rosas to reserve/futures deal|author=Benton, Dan|website=GiantsWire.USAToday.com|date=January 19, 2017|access-date=June 17, 2017}}</ref> Rosas was the only kicker on the Giants roster after former Giants' [[placekicker]] [[Robbie Gould]] agreed to a two-year contract with the [[San Francisco 49ers]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2697134-san-francisco-49ers-robbie-gould-reportedly-agree-to-contract|title=San Francisco 49ers, Robbie Gould Reportedly Agree to Contract|last=Conway|first=Tyler|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=April 10, 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=April 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180411111530/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2697134-san-francisco-49ers-robbie-gould-reportedly-agree-to-contract|url-status=live}}</ref> until veteran [[Mike Nugent]] signed a contract with the team on August 1.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-veteran-kicker-mike-nugent-19092653|title=Giants sign veteran kicker Mike Nugent|access-date=August 30, 2017|archive-date=March 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308002936/https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-veteran-kicker-mike-nugent-19092653|url-status=live}}</ref> Rosas ultimately won the starting kicker job after Nugent was released during final roster cuts.

On September 10, in the Giants' season-opening 19–3 loss to the [[2017 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], Rosas converted his first NFL career [[field goal]], a 25-yard attempt, in the third quarter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100dal.htm|title=New York Giants at Dallas Cowboys - September 10th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=September 14, 2017|archive-date=September 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914220331/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100dal.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> Prior to the game, he watched his girlfriend, Tiffany Lopez, give birth via [[FaceTime]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/09/14/giants-aldrick-rosas-watched-daughters-birth-on-facetime-then-made-nfl-debut/ | title=Giants' Aldrick Rosas watched daughter's birth on FaceTime, then made NFL debut | publisher=profootballtalk.nbcsports.com | date=September 14, 2017 | access-date=October 17, 2017 | author=Smith, Michael David | archive-date=October 18, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018072331/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/09/14/giants-aldrick-rosas-watched-daughters-birth-on-facetime-then-made-nfl-debut/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

Rosas finished the season with a 72% field goal conversion rate (31st in the league) and an 87% [[Conversion (gridiron football)|point after touchdown]] (PAT) conversion rate (last in the league).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/patriciatraina/2018/09/13/__trashed/#11c2eabd34a6|title=After Rough First Season, Giants' Aldrick Rosas Is In A Better Place Mentally|website=Forbes|language=en|access-date=October 2, 2018|archive-date=October 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002220007/https://www.forbes.com/sites/patriciatraina/2018/09/13/__trashed/#11c2eabd34a6|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== 2018 season ====
Rosas retained his starting job with the Giants for the 2018 season. He vastly improved on his rookie season, converting 32 of 33 field goal attempts and 31 of 32 PATs, with his only missed PAT due to a poor snap. He was named [[National Football Conference|NFC]] Special Teams Player of the Week for his Week 13 performance against the [[Chicago Bears]] where he converted three field goals, including a [[New York Giants]] franchise record 57-yarder and the game-winning 44-yard field goal in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nflcommunications.com/Pages/AFC-and-NFC-Players-of-the-Week---Week-12------------.aspx|title=AFC and NFC Players of the Week - Week 13|website=NFL.com|language=en|access-date=December 6, 2018|archive-date=December 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206234943/https://nflcommunications.com/Pages/AFC-and-NFC-Players-of-the-Week---Week-12------------.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref>

On December 18, 2018, Rosas was named to his first Pro Bowl,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.giants.com/news/saquon-barkley-landon-collins-and-aldrick-rosas-make-2018-pro-bowl|title=Saquon Barkley, Landon Collins, and Aldrick Rosas make 2018 Pro Bowl|website=Giants.com|language=en|access-date=January 7, 2019|archive-date=December 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219182540/https://www.giants.com/news/saquon-barkley-landon-collins-and-aldrick-rosas-make-2018-pro-bowl|url-status=live}}</ref> and on January 4, 2019, Rosas was named a Second-team [[All-Pro]] for 2018.

second-round tender on K Aldrick Rosas|website=Giants.com|language=en-US|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> and signed it on April 8.<ref>{{cite news |author=Salomone, Dan |title=K Aldrick Rosas signs '''Alexander Armah Jr.''' (born May 17, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Georgia Wolves football|West Georgia Wolves]] and was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in sixth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. Armah was also a member of the [[New Orleans Saints]] and [[Washington Commanders]].

==Early life==
Armah attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Dacula High School]] in [[Dacula, Georgia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Paul |date=May 8, 2017 |title=Dacula's Alex Armah took an unlikely path to the NFL |url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/professional/dacula-s-alex-armah-took-an-unlikely-path-to-the/article_c3e3edfd-beca-56f4-88cd-abdf1a445273.html |access-date=March 29, 2019 |website=[[Gwinnett Daily Post]] |language=en}}</ref> Armah attended and played [[college football]] at the [[University of West Georgia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Armah Bio |url=http://www.uwgsports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211697742&DB_OEM_ID=24310 |access-date=March 29, 2019 |website=UWGSports.com}}</ref>
