===Carolina Panthers===
Armah was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the sixth round, 192nd overall, in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Voth |first=Bill |date=April 29, 2017 |title=Panthers draft Alex Armah in sixth round |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-draft-Alex-Armah-in-sixth-round/fdba2608-f926-4c07-96c8-4895a652e9e7 |access-date=May 4, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=February 10, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was waived by the Panthers on September 3, 2017, and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson, Max |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Panthers claim Brad Kaaya and Demetrious Cox |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-claim-Brad-Kaaya-and-Demetrious-Cox/74b9ed41-5f37-4ce3-b8f1-b6d973c85fad |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010225712/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-claim-Brad-Kaaya-and-Demetrious-Cox/74b9ed41-5f37-4ce3-b8f1-b6d973c85fad |archive-date=October 10, 2017 |access-date=September 4, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He played in nine games his rookie season, and did not record any statistics. For the 2018 season, he survived training camp roster cuts and was named to the active roster. He made his 2018 debut in the season opener against the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. In the 16–8 victory, he scored his first career touchdown on a one-yard rush on his lone carry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scott |first=Jelani |date=September 9, 2018 |title=Panthers open season with 16-8 win over Cowboys |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-open-season-with-16-8-win-over-cowboys |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=Carolina Panthers |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson, Max |date=September 19, 2017 |title=Panthers place Greg Olsen on injured reserve |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-place-Greg-Olsen-on-injured-reserve/eed0e36a-4ee3-47e6-8090-ce6aab1df7d7 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171022172336/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-place-Greg-Olsen-on-injured-reserve/eed0e36a-4ee3-47e6-8090-ce6aab1df7d7 |archive-date=October 22, 2017 |access-date=September 20, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> On November 4, 2018, Armah scored his second career touchdown against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He appeared in all 16 games for 2018 season, mainly used as a blocking fullback and a special teamer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Armah 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmaAl00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=March 29, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2019 season, he appeared in all 16 games and recorded six carries for 11 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Armah 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmaAl00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alek Torgersen''' (born January 13, 1995) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]]. He played college football at [[Penn Quakers football|Penn]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/draft/2017/profiles/alek-torgersen?id=2558072|title=2017 NFL Draft Profile: Alek Torgersen|website=NFL.com|access-date=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
=== Atlanta Falcons ===
Torgersen signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an undrafted free agent on May 1, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons Agree To Terms With 21 CFAs|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-Agree-to-Terms-With-21-CFAs/1dbd9631-8b92-4405-8d9b-71fa59a85946|author=Jackson, Curtis|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=May 1, 2017|accessdate=May 28, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Falcons on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=2017 Atlanta Falcons Roster Cuts Tracker: Deadline To 53 Is 4 P.M. ET On Saturday|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/2017-Atlanta-Falcons-roster-cuts-tracker-Deadline-to-53-is-4-pm-ET-on-Saturday/98e7c2c6-e5e5-414f-bf3a-69e3863e701a|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230165513/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/2017-Atlanta-Falcons-roster-cuts-tracker-Deadline-to-53-is-4-pm-ET-on-Saturday/98e7c2c6-e5e5-414f-bf3a-69e3863e701a|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 30, 2017|author=Conway, Kelsey|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=September 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On September 4, 2017, Torgersen was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Add Three More Players To The Practice Squad|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Add-Three-More-Players-To-The-Practice-Squad/a88bac0a-041e-4402-86b0-130660ebaf92|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171012160458/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Add-Three-More-Players-To-The-Practice-Squad/a88bac0a-041e-4402-86b0-130660ebaf92|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 12, 2017|author=Czarda, Stephen|website=Redskins.com|date=September 4, 2017}}</ref> He was released on October 3, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign Joel Stave, Jerry Ugokwe To Practice Squad|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Joel-Stave-Jerry-Ugokwe-To-Practice-Squad/936d2e55-ff47-4bca-979a-f669ab9d9a4d|author=Czarda, Stephen|website=Redskins.com|date=October 3, 2017|access-date=October 4, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171004002542/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Joel-Stave-Jerry-Ugokwe-To-Practice-Squad/936d2e55-ff47-4bca-979a-f669ab9d9a4d|archive-date=October 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On December 27, 2017, Torgersen was signed to the [[Detroit Lions]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last=Birkett |first=Dave |date=December 27, 2017 |title=Detroit Lions sign QB Alek Torgersen to practice squad |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2017/12/27/detroit-lions-quarterback-alek-torgersen-practice-squad/984576001/ |access-date=September 12, 2025 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Lions on January 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions report 10 Reserve-Future signings|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-report-10-Reserve-Future-signings/d21eb71a-768f-4706-a0da-dc3f6f922c1a|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206084919/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-report-10-Reserve-Future-signings/d21eb71a-768f-4706-a0da-dc3f6f922c1a|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 6, 2018|website=DetroitLions.com|date=January 1, 2018}}</ref>

On April 4, 2018, he was waived by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alek Torgersen: Waived by Lions|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alek-torgersen-waived-by-lions/ |website= cbssports.com|date=April 5, 2018 |accessdate= April 5, 2018}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On April 5, 2018, Torgersen was claimed off waivers by the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cards Claim QBs Alek Torgersen, Brandon Doughty|url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cards-Claim-QBs-Alek-Torgersen-Brandon-Doughty/c5e51774-2def-4756-bf78-646c7a0a8ec6|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=April 5, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on May 7, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Cut-QBs-Brandon-Doughty-Alek-Torgersen/2ceebe56-f465-4ad7-8b5c-193e651a0b60|title=Cardinals Cut QBs Brandon Doughty, Alek Torgersen|last=Urban|first=Darren|date=May 7, 2018|work=AZCardinals.com|access-date=May 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507222722/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Cut-QBs-Brandon-Doughty-Alek-Torgersen/2ceebe56-f465-4ad7-8b5c-193e651a0b60|archive-date=May 7, 2018|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===Arizona Hotshots===
On August 6, 2018, Torgersen signed with the [[Arizona Hotshots]] of the [[Alliance of American Football|AAF]] for the 2019 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/football/2018/08/17/alliance-american-football-demario-richard-alek-torgersen-sign-phoenix/1021536002/|title=Former ASU, Arizona Cardinals players join Alliance of American football team in Phoenix|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=August 17, 2018|accessdate=November 29, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Scott|first=Dana|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/football/2018/10/31/aaf-hold-new-protect-pick-quarterback-draft/1835643002/|title=Alliance of American Football league to hold 'Protect or Pick' quarterback draft|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=October 31, 2018|accessdate=November 29, 2018}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Iron ===
Torgersen was drafted by the [[Birmingham Iron]] on November 27, 2018 in the [[2019 AAF QB Draft]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Margolis|first=Marc|url=https://www.thedp.com/article/2018/11/penn-football-alek-torgersen-quarterback-draft-alliance-of-american-football|title=Former Penn quarterback Alek Torgersen selected in Alliance of American Football draft|newspaper=[[The Daily Pennsylvanian]]|date=November 29, 2018|accessdate=November 29, 2018}}</ref> He was waived by the Iron on January 15, 2019, before the start of the regular season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Birmingham Iron Daily Report |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/birmingham-iron-daily-report/n-5438376 |website=oursportscentral.com |date=January 16, 2019 |accessdate=2019-02-12}}</ref>

=== San Diego Fleet ===
During the [[2019 AAF season]], Torgersen was picked up by the [[San Diego Fleet]] after starting quarterback [[Philip Nelson (American football)|Philip Nelson]] was placed on injured reserve on March 4.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gartin|first=Zachary|url=https://eastvillagetimes.com/2019/03/san-diego-fleet-make-a-flurry-of-roster-moves-in-response-to-injuries/|title=San Diego Fleet Make a Flurry of Roster Moves in Response to Injuries|publisher=East Village Times|date=March 4, 2019|accessdate=March 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044734/https://eastvillagetimes.com/2019/03/san-diego-fleet-make-a-flurry-of-roster-moves-in-response-to-injuries/|archive-date=March 6, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

'''Albert Chukwuemeka Okwuegbunam Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|oʊ|k|w|u|'|eɪ|b|u|n|ɑː|m}} {{respell|OH|kwoo|AY|boo|nahm}};<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuciQ7HSV3E&t=20s|title=Albert Okwuegbunam: Path to the Pros 2020|date=April 9, 2020|website=Youtube|access-date=August 18, 2022}}</ref> born April 25, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] for the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]] and was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in the fourth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Okwuegbunam attended [[Sacred Heart-Griffin High School]] in [[Springfield, Illinois]].<ref name="lincolncourier">{{Cite web |last=Mahan |first=Ryan |date=August 22, 2015 |title=CS8 football preview: Albert Okwuegbunam stands tall for loaded SHG |url=https://www.sj-r.com/article/20150822/SPORTS/150829853 |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=[[The State Journal-Register]] |publisher=[[GateHouse Media]]}}</ref> He played [[wide receiver]] for the [[high school football|football]] team. He committed to the [[University of Missouri]] to play [[college football]].<ref name="sj-r">{{Cite web |last=Webster |first=Brian |date=September 19, 2015 |title=SHG receiver Albert Okwuegbunam makes verbal commitment to Missouri |url=http://www.sj-r.com/article/20150919/SPORTS/150919418 |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=[[The State Journal-Register]] |publisher=[[GateHouse Media]]}}</ref>

==College career==
After redshirting his first year at Missouri in 2016, Okwuegbunam played in all 13 games in 2017 and recorded 29 receptions for 415 yards and 11 [[touchdowns]].<ref name="stltoday">{{Cite web |last=Matter |first=Dave |date=August 2, 2018 |title=Matter's Mizzou camp countdown: What can Albert O. do for an encore? |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/matter-s-mizzou-camp-countdown-what-can-albert-o-do/article_0543deb6-0278-54d7-87ac-34589ff832ee.html |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |publisher=[[Lee Enterprises]]}}</ref><ref name="stltoday2">{{Cite web |last=Matter |first=Dave |date=October 25, 2017 |title='Albert O' soars into spotlight for Mizzou |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/albert-o-soars-into-spotlight-for-mizzou/article_90bbb34c-0115-5fc2-96a7-ddffc120fe3b.html |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |publisher=[[Lee Enterprises]]}}</ref> He returned as Missouri's starter in 2018.<ref name="columbiamissourian">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Eric |date=August 4, 2018 |title=NOTEBOOK: Okwuegbunam looks to build on freshman campaign | Mizzou Football |url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_football/notebook-okwuegbunam-looks-to-build-on-freshman-campaign/article_d4d4bcb4-982b-11e8-b2ed-1f6ecd356169.html |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=[[Columbia Missourian]]}}</ref><ref name="columbiatribune">{{Cite web |last=Teague-Robinson |first=Cameron |date=August 25, 2018 |title=The big 'O' in Missouri's offense |url=http://www.columbiatribune.com/sports/20180825/big-o-in-missouris-offense |access-date=October 21, 2018 |website=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]] |publisher=[[GateHouse Media]]}}</ref> Following the 2019 season, Okwuegbunam decided to forgo his final year of eligibility and declared for the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terada, Souic |date=December 2, 2019 |title=Mizzou tight end Albert Okwuegbunam declares for NFL, leaves one year early |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article237955054.html |access-date=December 17, 2019 |website=kansascity.com}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
Okwuegbunam was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the fourth round with the 118th overall pick in the [[2020 NFL draft]], reuniting with his former Missouri teammate, [[Drew Lock]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murry |first=Thomas |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Denver Broncos draft Mizzou's Albert Okwuegbunam |work=ABC 17 |url=https://abc17news.com/news/2020/04/25/denver-broncos-draft-mizzous-albert-okwuegbunam/ |access-date=April 27, 2020}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in Week 6 of the season against the [[2020 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. He had two receptions for 45 yards in the 18–12 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at New England Patriots - October 18th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010180nwe.htm |access-date=October 22, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 10, 2020, with a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=November 10, 2020 |title=Broncos awarded CB De'Vante Bausby off waivers |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-awarded-cb-de-vante-bausby-off-waivers |access-date=October 8, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

On October 9, 2021, Okwuegbunam was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=October 9, 2021 |title=Broncos activate CB Ronald Darby from injured reserve |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-cb-ronald-darby-from-injured-reserve |access-date=October 8, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He was activated on October 30.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=October 30, 2021 |title=Broncos activate WR Jerry Jeudy, TE Albert Okwuegbunam, ILB Jonas Griffith from IR to 53-man roster |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-wr-jerry-jeudy-te-albert-okwuegbunam-ilb-jonas-griffith-from-ir |access-date=October 8, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

In 2022, Okwuegbunam played in 8 games for Denver, catching 10 passes for 95 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Albert Okwuegbunam 2022 Stats|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/4035115/albert-okwuegbunam|access-date=October 10, 2023|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On August 29, 2023, Okwuegbunam was traded to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] along with a 2025 seventh round pick for the Eagles’ 2025 sixth round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Broncos trade Albert Okwuegbunam to Eagles instead of waiving him |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/broncos-trade-albert-okwuegbunam-to-eagles-instead-of-waiving-him |access-date=August 29, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

On February 23, 2024, Okwuegbunam signed a one-year contract extension with the Eagles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=Owen |date=February 23, 2024 |title=Eagles sign Albert Okwuegbunam to contract extension |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-albert-okwuegbunam-to-contract-extension |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 27.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Get your first look at the Eagles' initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-53-man-roster-2024-season-jalen-hurts-saquon-barkley |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Okwuegbunam was released by the Eagles on November 5.<ref name="i685">{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Eagles release Albert Okwuegbunam | website=NBC Sports | date=2024-11-05 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/eagles-release-albert-okwuegbunam | access-date=2024-11-16}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On December 17, 2024, Okwuegbunam was signed to the [[Indianapolis Colts]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 17, 2024 |title=Colts sign TE Albert Okwuegbunam Jr. to practice squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-te-albert-okwuegbunam-to-practice-squad |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Colts on January 6, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 6, 2025 |title=Colts sign RB Tyler Goodson, LB Segun Olubi to 1-year contract extensions, sign 14 players to reserve/future contracts |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-rb-tyler-goodson-lb-segun-olubi-to-1-year-contract-extensions-sign-14-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> 

On July 31, 2025, Okwuegbunam was released by the Colts.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Arthur|first=Jake|title=Colts End Defender's Season, Sign Two Free Agents |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/colts/news/colts-end-defender-season-sign-free-agents |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=July 31, 2025 |access-date=July 31, 2025}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On August 3, 2025, Okwuegbunam signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders sign WR Kawaan Baker and TE Albert Okwuegbunam |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-wr-kawaan-baker-and-te-albert-okwuegbunam |website=Raiders.com |access-date=4 August 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders announce 2025 practice squad additions |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-2025-practice-squad-additions-roster-nfl-transactions |website=Raiders.com |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders make moves to bring roster to 53-player limit for 2025 season |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/las-vegas-raiders-53-man-roster-cuts-2025-season-nfl-transactions |website=Raiders.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref> Okwuegbunam signed a reserve/future contract with Las Vegas on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders announce 12 Reserve/Future signings|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announced-12-reserve-future-signings-2026-nfl-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=January 5, 2026}}</ref>

'''Alec Ingold''' (born July 9, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]].

==Early life==
Originally, Ingold committed to [[Northern Illinois Huskies football|Northern Illinois]] to play quarterback, but later accepted a scholarship from Wisconsin as an undecided athlete.<ref name="Hodkiewicz">{{Cite web |last=Hodkiewicz |first=Wes |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Alec Ingold is one step away from his childhood dream |url=https://www.packers.com/news/alec-ingold-is-one-step-away-from-his-childhood-dream |access-date=April 22, 2019 |website=[[Green Bay Packers|Packers.com]]}}</ref> He was named the [[Associated Press]] Wisconsin Player of the Year and the [[Gatorade]] Wisconsin Player of the Year his senior year at [[Bay Port High School]] as a [[dual-threat quarterback]].<ref name="Wilde">{{Cite web |last=Wilde |first=Jason |date=March 3, 2019 |title=With Packers seeing the value in fullbacks, could former Badger Alec Ingold find his way home? |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/football/professional/with-packers-seeing-the-value-in-fullbacks-could-former-badger/article_2d11d168-f0ad-5956-9c9a-2ba11fa9c2e1.html |access-date=April 22, 2019 |website=Madison.com}}</ref> 

He earned his undergraduate degree from [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] and was later admitted to [[Master of Business Administration]] at [[Kelley School of Business]], [[Indiana University Bloomington]].<ref>{{cite web| url =https://blog.kelley.iu.edu/2021/02/05/kelley-student-up-for-nfls-walter-payton-man-of-the-year-another-is-playing-in-the-big-game/| title =Kelley student up for NFL's Walter Payton Man of the Year; Three suited up for the big game| date =February 5, 2021|publisher=[[Kelley School of Business]]|accessdate=21 May 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
Over his career at [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]], Ingold started eleven games, primarily at fullback his senior year.<ref name="Wilde" /> He was originally a linebacker before moving to running back due to an injury to [[Corey Clement]] and later moving to fullback before his sophomore season, spending two years splitting snaps with Austin Ramesh before taking over primary duties his senior season.<ref name="Venci" /> Ingold was primarily used in short-yardage situations such as goal line scenarios, scoring a high touchdown-to-carry ratio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potrykus |first=Jeff |date=August 6, 2018 |title=Alec Ingold, a valuable reserve for three seasons, wants full-time work in 2018 |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2018/08/06/badgers-alec-ingold-wants-all-around-fullback/913458002/ |access-date=April 22, 2019 |website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}}</ref>

After his senior season, Ingold was invited to the [[2019 Senior Bowl]].<ref name="Venci">{{Cite web |last=Venci |first=Scott |date=January 8, 2019 |title=Alec Ingold prepares for NFL draft, reflects on Wisconsin career |url=https://www.greenbaypressgazette.com/story/sports/2019/01/08/alec-ingold-prepares-nfl-draft-reflects-wisconsin-career/2512780002/ |access-date=April 22, 2019 |website=[[Green Bay Press-Gazette]]}}</ref> He was also the only true fullback invited to the 2019 [[NFL Scouting Combine]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Kelly |date=April 21, 2019 |title=Alec Ingold took unique path to pursue NFL dream |url=https://www.nbc26.com/sports/packers-on-the-clock/alec-ingold-took-unique-path-to-pursue-nfl-dream |access-date=April 22, 2019 |website=[[WGBA]]}}</ref> His combine numbers included a 4.89-second 40-yard dash, 16 bench press repetitions, a 34-inch vertical jump and a 116-inch broad jump.<ref name="Wilde" />

===Oakland / Las Vegas Raiders===
Ingold signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent on May 3, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2019 |title=Raiders announce undrafted free agent signings |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-undrafted-free-agent-signings |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=Raiders.com |archive-date=May 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190504183937/https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-undrafted-free-agent-signings |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ingold made his first start for the Raiders on ''Monday Night Football'' against the [[Denver Broncos]] on September 9.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Oakland Raiders - September 9th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909090rai.htm |access-date=January 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Ingold scored his first career touchdown on Week 10, in a 26–24 victory of the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers at Oakland Raiders - November 7th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911070rai.htm |access-date=January 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He caught three passes for 22 yards in a 20-16 loss to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in Week 15.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 7, 2019 |title=Oakland Raiders score late to edge Los Angeles Chargers |url=https://www.tsn.ca/raiders-rally-to-beat-chargers-26-24-1.1394501 |access-date=November 8, 2019 |website=TSN.ca |language=en}}</ref>

On September 21, 2020 on ''Monday Night Football'' against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Ingold caught the first Raiders touchdown in [[Allegiant Stadium]] history in the 34–24 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williamson |first=Bill |date=September 21, 2020 |title=Raiders fullback Alec Ingold makes history with first Las Vegas TD at Allegiant Stadium |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2020/9/21/21450190/raiders-fullback-alec-ingold-history-first-touchdown-allegiant-stadium |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=Silver And Black Pride |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Las Vegas Raiders - September 21st, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009210rai.htm |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
In 2020, Ingold was the Las Vegas Raiders nominee for the Walter Payton Man of the Year Award.

In Week 10 of the 2021 season, Ingold suffered a torn ACL and was ruled out for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Damien |first=Levi |date=November 20, 2021 |title=Raiders send FB Alec Ingold to injured reserve, activate S Roderic Teamer from IR |url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2021/11/20/raiders-send-fb-alec-ingold-to-injured-reserve-activate-s-roderic-teamer-from-ir/ |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=Raiders Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On March 17, 2022, Ingold signed a two-year, $6.5 million contract with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Dolphins sign FB Ingold |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/roster-moves-dolphins-sign-fb-ingold |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref>

On August 31, 2023, Ingold signed a three-year contract extension with the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Miami Dolphins Sign Ingold to Contract Extension|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-sign-ingold-to-contract-extension|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=August 31, 2023}}</ref>

On March 6, 2026, Ingold was released by the Dolphins following a head coaching change from [[Mike McDaniel]], the head coach of the Dolphins when Ingold was signed, to former [[Green Bay Packers]] defensive coordinator [[Jeff Hafley]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins make roster moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-x3827 |website=miamidolphins.com |access-date=7 March 2026}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On March 8, 2026, Ingold signed a two-year, $7.5 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Agree to Terms with Pro Bowl Fullback Alec Ingold|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/agree-to-terms-pro-bowl-fullback-alec-ingold-2026|website=Chargers.com|date=March 8, 2026}}</ref> Ingold's signing with the Chargers came after the Chargers hired coach Mike McDaniel, the head coach and main offensive play-caller of the Miami Dolphins during Ingold's tenure with the team, as their [[offensive coordinator]]. <ref>https://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/dolphins/2026/03/08/nfl-free-agency-former-dolphins-alec-ingold-signs-with-chargers-reunites-mike-mcdaniel/89059507007/</ref>

==Personal life==
Ingold is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Romano |first=Jason |date=June 28, 2023 |title=SS PODCAST: Dolphins fullback Alec Ingold on adversity, opportunity, faith |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/podcast/2023/06/28/podcast-dolphins-fullback-alec-ingold-faith-adversity/ |access-date=15 December 2023 |website=Sports Spectrum}}</ref> He is married to Alexa Ingold.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexa and Alec in Oconomowoc, WI |url=https://lovestoriestv.com/alexa-alec-wedding-video-june-2023 |access-date=15 December 2023}}</ref>

Ingold was adopted, and now helps to promote various organizations that raise awareness and help the adoption of children.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Habib |first1=Hal |title=Dolphins' Alec Ingold: 'Everyone deserves a loving family.' Here's how he found his |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/2022/12/03/dolphins-alec-ingold-discusses-his-adoption-joining-loving-family/10803192002/ |access-date=30 March 2023 |work=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |date=December 3, 2022}}</ref> During his time at Bay Port, Ingold was also a state champion wrestler, winning the 220-pound weight class in Division 1 as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2015 |title=Ingold goes the distance for first state title |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/ingold-goes-the-distance-for-first-state-title |access-date=May 7, 2020 |website=USA Today High School Sports |publisher=Gannett}}</ref>

Before his rookie NFL season, Ingold secured an internship at [[Oracle Corporation]] in the event that he did not make a final NFL roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Venci |first=Scott |date=September 4, 2019 |title= Dream realized: Bay Port's Alec Ingold makes the NFL |url=https://www.greenbaypressgazette.com/story/sports/2019/09/04/raiders-fullback-alec-ingold-former-bay-port-standout-reaches-nfl/2210951001/ |access-date=February 2, 2023 |website=Green Bay Press-Gazette |publisher=Gannett}}</ref>

'''Albert Huggins Jr.''' (born June 27, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). After playing [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]], he was signed by the [[Houston Texans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2019. He was also a member of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[New England Patriots]], [[Detroit Lions]], [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Dallas Cowboys]], and [[St. Louis Battlehawks]].

===Houston Texans (first stint)===
Huggins signed with the [[Houston Texans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 10, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 10, 2019 |title=Texans sign six draft picks, 20 college free agents |work=HoustonTexans.com |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-six-draft-picks-20-college-free-agents |accessdate=October 21, 2019}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on August 31, 2019,<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Texans trim roster to 53 players |work=HoustonTexans.com |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-trim-roster-to-53-players |accessdate=October 21, 2019 |archive-date=September 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901032100/https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-trim-roster-to-53-players |url-status=dead }}</ref> but was signed to the team's [[practice squad]] on September 2.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 2, 2019 |title=Texans sign CB Armstrong, TE Paulsen, add 10 players to practice squad |work=HoustonTexans.com |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-cb-armstrong-te-paulsen-add-10-players-to-practice-squad |accessdate=October 21, 2019 |archive-date=September 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903055615/https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-cb-armstrong-te-paulsen-add-10-players-to-practice-squad |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 21, 2019, Huggins was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] off the Texans' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson, Chris |date=October 21, 2019 |title=Eagles agree to sign DTs Anthony Rush and Albert Huggins, release CB Orlando Scandrick and DT Akeem Spence |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-sign-anthony-rush-release-orlando-scandrick-akeem-spence |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was waived after playing in four games on November 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McPherson, Chris |date=November 30, 2019 |title=Roster moves: Eagles activate CB Cre'Von LeBlanc, promote TE Joshua Perkins from the practice squad |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/roster-moves-eagles-activate-cb-crevon-leblanc-promote-te-joshua-perkins |accessdate=November 30, 2019}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On December 2, 2019, Huggins was claimed off waivers by the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2019 |title=Patriots claim DL Albert Huggins from Philadelphia; Release K Kai Forbath |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-claim-dl-albert-huggins-from-philadelphia-release-k-kai-forbath |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> He was waived on December 7, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael |date=December 7, 2019 |title=Albert Huggins cut, Nick Folk back for Patriots |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/12/07/albert-huggins-cut-nick-folk-back-for-patriots/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com |publisher=NBC Sports |accessdate=December 22, 2019}}</ref>

===Houston Texans (second stint)===

===Detroit Lions (second stint)===

===New Orleans Saints===
On May 6, 2021, Huggins signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 6, 2021 |title=New Orleans Saints sign DT Albert Huggins |work=NewOrleansSaints.com |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-sign-defensive-tackle-albert-huggins-roster-moves-2021 |access-date=May 6, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2021, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints make roster reductions to 53|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-make-roster-reductions-to-53-2021|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce practice squad additions|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-2021-practice-squad-additions-roster|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref> Huggins was signed to the active roster on September 11, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-x0254|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=September 11, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on October 25 and re-signed to the practice squad. He was promoted to the active roster on December 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves ahead of Dallas Cowboys game {{!}} NFL Week 13|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-ahead-of-dallas-cowboys-game-nfl-week-1|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=December 2, 2021}}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, Huggins was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints make roster reductions to 53|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-reductions-to-53-2022-nfl-season|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref> He spent the entire 2022 season on the IR with an undisclosed injury he suffered during the Saints’ final preseason game. '''Alex Bachman''' (born May 29, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]]  [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]].

==College career==
Bachman was a member of the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] for four seasons. As a senior, he caught 37 passes for 541 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vcstar.com/story/sports/nfl/rams/2019/06/07/back-home-alex-bachman-making-adjustment-nfl/1321182001/|title=Back home in Thousand Oaks, Alex Bachman is making the adjustment to the NFL with the Rams|work=[[Ventura County Star]]|date=June 7, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref> Bachman finished his collegiate career with 82 receptions for 1,162 yards and ten touchdowns in 32 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants/news/new-york-giants-receivers-david-sills-v-and-alex-bachman-turning-heads-in-camp|title=Receivers David Sills V and Alex Bachman Turning Heads in Camp|first=Patricia|last=Traina|website=SI.com|date=August 24, 2020|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
Bachman was signed by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] as an undrafted free agent on April 29, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/la-sp-rams-20190429-story.html|title=Rams sign 14 undrafted free agents to bolster roster|date=April 29, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref> He was waived/injured during final roster cuts on August 31,<ref>{{cite news |author=Han, Jamie |title=Rams trim roster down to 53 players |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-trim-roster-down-to-53-players |website=TheRams.com |date=August 31, 2019 |accessdate=October 25, 2020}}</ref> and reverted to [[injured reserve]] the next day.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rams' Alex Bachman: Hits IR |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/rams-alex-bachman-hits-ir/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=September 1, 2019 |accessdate=October 25, 2020}}</ref> Bachman was waived by the Rams with an injury settlement on September 5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/rams-waive-wr-alex-bachman-from-ir-with-settlement/|title=Rams waive WR Alex Bachman from IR with Settlement|first=Nate|last=Bouda|website=NFLTradeRumors.co|date=September 6, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref>

2 spots open |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-roster-sign-13-players-to-practice-squad-2-spots-open |website=Giants.com |date=September 6, 2020 |accessdate=October 25, 2020}}</ref> He was released on September 15,<ref>{{cite news |author=Eisen, Michael |title=Judge pleased with effort, but corrections needed |url=https://www.giants.com/news/joe-judge-offensive-line-andrew-thomas-nick-gates-cam-fleming-steelers-week-one |website=Giants.com |date=September 15, 2020 |accessdate=October 25, 2020}}</ref> but he was re-signed to the practice squad on October 5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/06/new-york-giants-shuffle-practice-squad-re-sign-wr-alex-bachman/|title=Giants shuffle practice squad, re-sign WR Alex Bachman|first=Dan|last=Benton|website=Giants Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=October 6, 2020|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref> Bachman was elevated to the active roster on October 22 and made his NFL debut on that night in a 22–21 loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-alex-bachman-elevated-from-practice-squad/|title=Giants' Alex Bachman: Elevated from practice squad|website=CBSSports.com|publisher=RotoWire|date=October 22, 2020|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.giants.com/news/notes-stats-inside-thursday-night-s-loss-to-eagles-daniel-jones-joe-judge|title=Notes & Stats: Inside Thursday night's loss to Eagles|first=Michael|last=Eisen|website=Giants.com|date=October 22, 2020|access-date=October 23, 2020}}</ref> He reverted to the practice squad after the game on October 23.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alex Bachman: Back to practice roster |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alex-bachman-back-to-practice-roster/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=October 24, 2020 |accessdate=October 25, 2020}}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, Bachman was waived by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster for 2022|url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-roster-2022-nfl-season-joe-schoen-brian-daboll|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On November 15, 2022, Bachman signed with the practice squad of the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-11-15-2022|title=Houston Texans Transactions (11-15-2022)|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=November 15, 2022}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Houston on January 10, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-10-2023)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-10-2023|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=January 10, 2023}}</ref> Bachman was waived on August 22.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (8-22-2023)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-8-22-2023|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=August 22, 2023}}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on November 8.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (11-08-2023)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-11-08-2023|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=November 8, 2023}}</ref> Bachman signed a reserve/future contract with the Texans on January 22, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (1-22-2024)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-1-22-2024|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=January 22, 2024}}</ref> He was waived by Houston on April 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (04-09-2024)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-04-09-2024|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=April 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On May 22, 2024, Bachman signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign WR Alex Bachman|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-wide-receiver-alex-bachman-nfl-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=May 22, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on August 27, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders make moves to bring roster to 53-player limit|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-make-moves-to-bring-roster-to-53-man-roster-nfl-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders announce practice squad additions|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-practice-squad-additions-nfl-roster-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 19.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Damien |first1=Levi |title=Raiders make 3 roster moves ahead of Week 7 vs Rams |url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2024/10/19/raiders-make-3-roster-moves-ahead-of-week-7-vs-rams/ |website=Raiders Wire |access-date=20 October 2024}}</ref> Bachman was waived by the Raiders on November 16, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alex Bachman: Let go by Las Vegas |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alex-bachman-let-go-by-las-vegas/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=17 November 2024}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Raiders on January 23, 2025.

On August 26, 2025, Bachman was released by the Raiders as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders make moves to bring roster to 53-player limit for 2025 season |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/las-vegas-raiders-53-man-roster-cuts-2025-season-nfl-transactions |website=raiders.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders announce 2025 practice squad additions |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-2025-practice-squad-additions-roster-nfl-transactions |website=raiders.com |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on October 3.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders sign WR Alex Bachman to active roster, place LB Brennan Jackson on Reserve/Injured list |url=http://raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-wr-alex-bachman-to-active-roster-place-lb-brennan-jackson-on-reserve-injured-list |website=raiders.com |access-date=4 October 2025}}</ref>

'''Alan Keith Pringle''' (born January 20, 1952) is a Venezuelan-born former [[American football]] [[placekicker]] who played one game in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Detroit Lions]]. Born in [[Venezuela]], he played [[college football]] for the [[Rice Owls football|Rice Owls]] and was also a member of the [[Houston Oilers]] and [[New England Patriots]].
==Early and personal life==
Pringle was born on January 20, 1952, in [[Punto Fijo|Los Taques, Venezuela]], and spent his early years in [[Caracas]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/p/prin00800.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Alan Pringle Stats}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/44003753/?match=2&terms=alan%20pringle%20caracas|newspaper=[[Irving Daily News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 1, 1971|page=15|title=SWC has variety of opponents|url-access=subscription}}</ref> His parents were from England.<ref name="auto6">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/633124033/?match=2&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 26, 1973|page=31|title=Owls' Pringle Finds Himself|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He later moved to England, where he attended [[Rugby High School for Girls|Rugby High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PrinAl20.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Alan Pringle Stats}}</ref> He grew up playing [[Association football|soccer]] and [[Rugby football|rugby]].<ref name="auto5">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/961665642/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=June 20, 1975|page=19|title=Pringle Primed for Stars|author=Randall, Keith|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Pringle is, along with fellow [[placekicker]] [[Pat Ragusa]], [[José Borregales]], and [[Andrés Borregales]], one of only four Venezuelan-born [[National Football League]] (NFL) players.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/friv/birthplaces.cgi?country=Venezuela|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=List of all NFL Players Born in Venezuela}}</ref> Pringle married Ann Dillard in 1974.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/757082163/?match=4&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Corpus Christi Caller-Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=May 26, 1974|page=84|url-access=subscription|title=Pringle-Dillard}}</ref>

==College career==
Pringle later moved to the United States to attend [[Rice University]].<ref name="auto6"/> As a [[freshman]] at Rice in 1970, he was noticed by an assistant coach for the [[Rice Owls football]] team, who saw him kicking a soccer ball at a P.E. class.<ref name="auto6"/><ref name="auto2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1008164209/?match=7&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[The Orange Leader (Texas)|The Orange Leader]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 29, 1974|page=7|title=Owls' Pringle Man of Action|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was invited to tryout for the team and "was shown a [[Ball (gridiron football)|football]] and told to kick it through the [[Goal (sports)#Gridiron football|uprights]]."<ref name="auto5"/><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/58583947/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[San Antonio Express]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=June 22, 1975|page=55|title=East fights back, wins, 23-21|author=Cook, Dan|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He recalled "That was on a Tuesday. On Thursday I kicked for some more coaches and on Friday I was playing against [[Wharton Junior College]] in a [[Junior varsity|JV]] game."<ref name="auto5"/>

Pringle's first appearance was the first American football game he had ever seen.<ref name="auto6"/> "They told me when someone yelled '[[touchdown]]' I was supposed to go in and kick," he said.<ref name="auto6"/> He showed inexperience in his first game, however, mistiming his [[Kickoff (gridiron football)|kickoffs]] and wearing backwards [[Protective equipment in gridiron football#Hip, tail, thigh, and knee pads|hip pads]].<ref name="auto5"/> He later improved and set a school record for the freshman team that year with a 48-yard [[field goal]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/214700443/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[The Times (Shreveport)|The Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 14, 1970|page=23|title=Rice, 16-5|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Pringle made the varsity team for the 1971 season but was dismissed from the team early on for disciplinary reasons.<ref name="auto4">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/643472149/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 15, 1971|page=40|title=Owl Kicker Dismissed|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> By that point, he had made all five [[Conversion (gridiron football)|extra point]] attempts and tied the school record with a 48-yard field goal.<ref name="auto4"/> Afterwards, Pringle dropped out of school for a year.<ref name="auto6"/> During this time, he said that he just "piddled around" and "was living on crackers and peanut butter."<ref name="auto6"/> In 1973, he returned to Rice and was given another chance on the football team.<ref name="auto6"/> He was the team's top kicker for the 1973 and 1974 seasons, setting a school-record with a 50-yard field goal in the latter year.<ref name="auto6"/><ref name="auto5"/><ref name="auto2"/> Pringle concluded his career at Rice having made 27 of 28 extra point attempts and 20 of 29 field goal attempts.<ref name="auto5"/> He was invited to the [[Coaches All-America Game]] where he set the all-star game's record with a 54-yard field goal.<ref name="auto5"/><ref name="auto"/>

==Professional career==
Pringle was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] in the 10th round (246th overall) of the [[1975 NFL draft]].<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/44909806/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Valley Morning Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 30, 1975|page=25|url-access=subscription|agency=[[Associated Press]]|title=Oiler Draftee Hardeman Spouts Poetry Like Ali}}</ref> He made two field goals in a preseason game against the [[New Orleans Saints]] and finished the preseason having made three of five field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/757220243/?match=4&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Corpus Christi Caller-Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 4, 1975|page=47|title=Three Oilers missing|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was released by the Oilers prior to the regular season, on September 2, 1975.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1008092793/?match=2&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[The Orange Leader (Texas)|The Orange Leader]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 10, 1975|page=8|title=Pringle Boosts Oilers To Sloppy Victory|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/p/prin00800.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Alan Pringle NFL Transactions}}</ref> He then tried out with the [[Detroit Lions]] and was signed by them on September 11.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/43639237/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Lincoln Journal Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 12, 1975|page=31|title=Lions Sign Kicker Pringle|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The Lions signed him to be a [[kickoff specialist]], as they already had [[Errol Mann]] for field goals and extra points.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1109418867/?match=2&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[The Saginaw News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 13, 1975|page=21|title=Lions picking through rejects to fill bench|agency=[[United Press International]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Pringle appeared for the Lions in the season opener, against the [[Green Bay Packers]], but was unable to consistently kick to the [[end zone]] and was released following the game on September 22.<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PrinAl20/gamelog/|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Alan Pringle Career Game Log}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1071169851/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[Martinsville Bulletin]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 9, 1975|page=20|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url-access=subscription|title=Andybody Have a Kicker for Lions?}}</ref> Pringle later signed with the [[New England Patriots]] on April 12, 1976, but was released on July 30, ending his professional career.<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/972407076/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[The Atlanta Journal]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 13, 1976|page=51|title=Pro Transactions|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/436182375/?match=1&terms=alan%20pringle|newspaper=[[The Boston Globe]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 31, 1976|page=27|title=Transactions|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

'''Alaric Jackson''' (born July 14, 1998) is a Canadian and American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]].

==Early life==
Jackson was born to  Al Sr. He grew up in [[Windsor, Ontario]] and spent summers in Detroit, Michigan near the areas of West Seven Mile and Schafer with his father known as Al Sr. before moving to [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]], and holds dual Canadian-American citizenship.<ref name="t297">{{cite web | last=Beacham | first=Greg | title=Alaric Jackson is getting a pricy homecoming in Detroit after his breakthrough season with the Rams | website=AP News | date=2024-01-12 | url=https://apnews.com/article/rams-lions-alaric-jackson-76da1409f9beaba7a8d26c012eaa140d | access-date=2024-12-10}}</ref><ref name=sun/> He attended [[Renaissance High School (Michigan)|Renaissance High School]], where he originally played basketball and did not start playing football until his junior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barrows |first=Pete |date=August 7, 2015 |title=Detroit Renaissance tackle Alaric Jackson bursts on the scene as a Division I recruit |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/detroit-renaissance-tackle-alaric-jakcson-bursts-on-the-scene-as-a-division-i-recruit/ |access-date=August 31, 2021 |website=[[MLive.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorsey |first=Matt |date=March 20, 2015 |title=Recruiting: MSU offers Renaissance OT Alaric Jackson |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2015/03/20/michigan-state-spartans-football-recruiting/25067533/ |access-date=August 31, 2021 |website=[[Detroit Free Press]]}}</ref> Jackson committed to play [[college football]] at Iowa over offers from Iowa State, Nebraska, and Michigan State.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hawkins |first=James |date=February 3, 2016 |title=Renaissance’s Alaric Jackson sticks with Iowa |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2016/02/03/renaissances-alaric-jackson-sticks-iowa/79751942/ |access-date=August 31, 2021 |website=[[The Detroit News]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Jackson [[redshirted]] his true freshman season.<ref name="sun">{{Cite web |last=Kryk |first=John |date=April 25, 2021 |title=Canadian NFL draft profile: Alaric Jackson of Windsor |url=https://torontosun.com/sports/football/nfl/canadian-nfl-draft-profile-alaric-jackson-of-windsor |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=[[Toronto Sun]]}}</ref> He started every regular season game for Iowa at left tackle during his redshirt freshman season and was named to the [[Big Ten Conference]] All-Freshman team and a freshman [[All-American]] by the [[Football Writers Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rittenberg |first=Adam |date=August 8, 2018 |title=Iowa's Alaric Jackson, Cedrick Lattimore suspended |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/24320292/iowa-alaric-jackson-cedrick-lattimore-suspended |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> Jackson missed the season opener of his sophomore season after being suspended for violating team rules, but started the final 12 games of the season and was named second-team All-Big Ten.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goricki |first=David |date=July 24, 2019 |title=From Detroit to Iowa to possible first-round NFL draft pick |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/big-ten/2019/07/24/alaric-jackson-detroit-iowa-possible-first-round-nfl-draft-pick/1815602001/ |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=[[The Detroit News]]}}</ref> He missed three games due to injury as a redshirt junior and was named third-team All-Big Ten at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 14, 2020 |title=Jackson anchors veteran Hawkeye offensive front |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/college/football/jackson-anchors-veteran-hawkeye-offensive-front/article_1db4b07e-cfb1-5ab4-a390-412e262b04a6.html |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=[[Quad-City Times]]}}</ref> As a redshirt senior, Jackson was named first-team All-Big Ten and a second-team All-American by the [[American Football Coaches Association]] after starting all eight of Iowa's games in the team's [[COVID-19]]-shortened [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2020 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 22, 2021 |title=Canadian Alaric Jackson performs for NFL scouts at Iowa's pro day |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nfl/article/canadian-alaric-jackson-performs-nfl-scouts-iowas-pro-day/ |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=[[Sportsnet.ca]] |publisher=[[Canadian Press]]}}</ref>

Jackson signed with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 3, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dochterman |first=Scott |date=May 3, 2021 |title=Where Iowa players landed in the 2021 NFL Draft and as free agents, how they fit and who could be next |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2562663/2021/05/03/where-iowa-players-landed-in-the-2021-nfl-draft-and-as-free-agents-how-they-fit-and-who-could-be-next/ |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref> He made the Rams' 53-man roster out of training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hlas |first=Mike |date=September 3, 2021 |title=Hawkeyes in the NFL |url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-football/hawkeyes-in-the-nfl/ |access-date=November 24, 2021 |website=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]}}</ref> Jackson made his NFL debut on October 31, 2021, playing nine snaps on offense in the fourth quarter of a 38–22 win over the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=November 1, 2021 |title=Rams Week 8 snap counts: Jones leads LBs, Long Jr. fills in for Rochell |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/lists/rams-week-8-snap-counts-texans-ernest-jones/ |access-date=November 24, 2021 |website=Rams Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Jackson won [[Super Bowl LVI]] when the Rams defeated the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] 23–20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVI - Los Angeles Rams vs. Cincinnati Bengals - February 13th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202202130cin.htm |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Jackson entered the 2022 season as a backup offensive lineman. He was named the starting right guard in Week 3 for four games, then moved to left tackle for two games due to injuries. He was diagnosed with blood clots and was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]] on November 16, 2022.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1593002208093962240 |user=RamsNFL |title=LA Rams Transactions: • Designated for Return, Returned to Practice G David Edwards • Reserve/Injured T Chandler Brewer, T Alaric Jackson, WR Cooper Kupp}}</ref>

Jackson was suspended the first two games of the 2024 season for violating the league's personal conduct policy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams T Alaric Jackson suspended two games for Personal Conduct Policy violation|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/rams-t-alaric-jackson-suspended-two-games-for-personal-conduct-policy-violation|author=Alper, Josh|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 23, 2024}}</ref>

On February 28, 2025, Jackson and the Rams agreed on a three-year, $57 million contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2025 |title=Source: Rams, Alaric Jackson reach 3-year, $57 million deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/44057296/rams-alaric-jackson-agree-3-year-57-million-deal |access-date=March 2, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Public scrutiny and legal issues ==
In November 2025, Jackson was named in a civil lawsuit filed in Los Angeles Superior Court by a woman who alleged he recorded her without her consent during sex and refused to delete the video despite her requests.<ref>{{cite news |last1=La Rose |first1=Adam |title=Rams LT Alaric Jackson Named In Civil Suit |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2025/11/rams-lt-alaric-jackson-named-in-civil-suit |work=ProFootballRumors |date=November 14, 2025}} </ref> The plaintiff claimed Jackson recorded her without her consent in May 2024, reported the incident to the NFL, and that the league subsequently suspended him for two games under its personal conduct policy for an undisclosed violation later linked to the suit’s allegations.<ref>{{cite news |last1=La Rose |first1=Adam |title=Rams LT Alaric Jackson Named In Civil Suit |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2025/11/rams-lt-alaric-jackson-named-in-civil-suit |work=ProFootballRumors |date=November 14, 2025}}</ref> Jackson and his representatives have declined detailed public comment due to ongoing legal proceedings. The lawsuit would eventually be moved to federal court, where it was dismissed on April 10, 2026.<ref name=chargeandlawsuitdismissal />

On June 8, 2026, Jackson was arrested on suspicion of felony domestic battery.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/rams-alaric-jackson-arrested-for-felony-domestic-battery|title=Rams’ Alaric Jackson arrested for felony domestic battery|first=Michael David|last=Smith|work=NBC Sports|date=June 9, 2026|accessdate=June 9, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/story/2026-06-09/rams-alaric-jackson-arrested-on-suspicion-of-felony-domestic-violence|title=Rams’ Alaric Jackson arrested on suspicion of felony domestic violence|first=Austin|last=Knoblauch|work=Los Angeles Times|date=June 9, 2026|accessdate=June 9, 2026}}</ref> On June 9, he would be booked after being charged with felony domestic violence, and was the same day released on a $50,000 bond.<ref name=chargeandlawsuitdismissal>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49010238/rams-alaric-jackson-arrested-domestic-violence-charge|title=Rams' Alaric Jackson arrested on domestic violence charge|first=Sarah|last=Barshop|work=ESPN|date=June 9, 2026|accessdate=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

'''Alec Joseph Pierce''' (born May 2, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]] before the Colts selected him in the second round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Pierce grew up in [[Glen Ellyn, Illinois]] and attended [[Glenbard West High School]], where he played football, volleyball, basketball and ran track.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stone |first=Bill |date=May 29, 2018 |title=Boys Track and Field: Alec Pierce's debut in track helps lead Hilltoppers to ninth at state |url=https://www.shawlocal.com/2018/05/29/boys-track-and-field-alec-pierces-debut-in-track-helps-lead-hilltoppers-to-ninth-at-state/aljgeml/ |access-date=October 5, 2021 |website=[[Shaw Media|ShawLocal.com]]}}</ref> His father, Greg Pierce, was a former [[tight end]] who played collegiately at [[Northwestern University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Atkins |first=Nate |date=August 15, 2023 |title=How Anthony Richardson and Alec Pierce Are Working on Their Deep-Ball Connection |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2023/08/15/colts-how-anthony-richardson-and-alec-pierce-are-working-on-deep-passes/70585405007/ |access-date=2023-09-16 |website=IndyStar.com}}</ref>

As a senior, Alec caught 25 passes for 372 yards and five touchdowns with three sacks and four interceptions on defense and was named the Most Valuable Player of the [[West Suburban Conference]] Silver Division.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Narang |first=Bob |date=December 13, 2017 |title=Football: Glenbard West WR Alec Pierce commits to Cincinnati |url=https://www.shawlocal.com/2017/12/13/football-glenbard-west-wr-alec-pierce-commits-to-cincinnati/auurvbq/ |access-date=October 5, 2021 |website=[[Shaw Media|ShawLocal.com]]}}</ref> Pierce was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Cincinnati over scholarship offers from 17 other programs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Halloran |first=Tim |date=December 12, 2017 |title=Recruiting news and notes: Glenbard West WR commits to Cincinnati |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/preps-talk/recruiting-news-and-notes-glenbard-west-wr-commits-cincinnati |access-date=October 5, 2021 |website=[[NBC Sports Chicago]]}}</ref>

Pierce was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the second round with the 53rd overall pick in the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2022/draft.htm |access-date=October 11, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=April 29, 2022 |title=NFL Draft 2022: Colts Select Cincinnati Wide Receiver Alec Pierce With No. 53 Overall Pick |url=https://www.colts.com/news/pick-alec-pierce-second-round-53rd-overall-wide-receiver-cincinnati |access-date=February 15, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> On October 16, Pierce caught his first career touchdown in the Week 6 matchup against the [[2022 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heltman |first=Russ |date=October 16, 2022 |title=Watch: Alec Pierce Scores Game-Winning TD Against Jaguars |url=https://www.si.com/college/cincinnati/football/watch-alec-pierce-scores-game-winning-td-against-jaguars |access-date=February 15, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> The Colts won the game 34–27.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts – October 16th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210160clt.htm |access-date=February 15, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Pierce posted his best NFL game on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football]]'', notching team-highs in catches (four) and receiving yards (86) while adding his second-career touchdown. He finished his rookie season with 41 receptions for 593 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Pierce 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PierAl00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2023-02-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

In Week 14 of the 2023 season against the [[2023 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], Pierce enjoyed his first career 100–yard game. He opened the game with a 36-yard touchdown on Indianapolis' first possession, and finished with 100 yards and a touchdown on six receptions.<ref>{{cite web | last=Moore | first=Raven | title=Why Wide receiver Alec Pierce's 100-yard receiving game against Titans was a testament to the importance of patience | website=Colts.com | date=2023-12-04 | url=https://www.colts.com/news/wide-receiver-alec-pierce-touchdown-tennessee-titans-michael-pittman-jr | access-date=2024-07-23}}</ref> Pierce finished the season as the Colts' third-leading receiver with 32 catches for 514 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Pierce 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PierAl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Indianapolis Colts Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/clt/2023.htm |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 1 of the 2024 season, Pierce had three receptions for 125 yards and a touchdown in a 29–27 loss to the [[2024 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Indianapolis Colts - September 8th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202409080clt.htm |access-date=2024-12-25 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In a Week 5 loss to the [[2024 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]], he had three receptions for 134 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars - October 6th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410060jax.htm |access-date=2024-12-25 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 17 against the [[2024 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], Pierce recorded six receptions for 122 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at New York Giants - December 29th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202412290nyg.htm |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2024 season, he had 37 receptions for 824 yards and seven touchdowns.

Pierce made 15 appearances (14 starts) for Indianapolis during the 2025 season, logging 47 receptions for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alec Pierce 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PierAl00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His 47 receptions were the fewest to clear 1,000 yards since [[DeSean Jackson]] did so in 2010.<ref>{{cite web | last=Ackerman | first=Sean | title=Colts' Alec Pierce Breaks Silence on Daniel Jones, What's Ahead | website=Indianapolis Colts On SI | date=February 18, 2026 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/colts/onsi/news/colts-alec-pierce-talks-daniel-jones-upcoming-offseason | access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref>

On March 12, 2026, Pierce re-signed with the Colts on a four-year, $114 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stankevitz |first1=JJ |date=March 11, 2026  |title=Colts re-sign WR Alec Pierce |url=https://www.colts.com/news/alec-pierce-officially-re-signed-new-contract-wide-receiver-nfl-free-agency |access-date=13 March 2026 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

'''Alex Akingbulu''' (born December 28, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Arlington Renegades|Dallas Renegades]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]] and [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=June 9, 2018 |title=Jackson Gibbs and Alex Akingbulu leaving UCLA football team |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-football-20180608-story.html |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Infante |first=Jared |date=January 25, 2022 |title=Meet Alex Akingbulu, Fresno State's breakout OL prospect |url=https://draftwire.usatoday.com/2022/01/25/2022-nfl-draft-prospects-alex-akingbulu-fresno-state-interview/ |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=The Draft Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> Akingbulu has also played for the [[Philadelphia Stars (2022)|Philadelphia Stars]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL).

'''Alan Nathan Kline''' (born May 25, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for one season with the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]].

==Early life and college==
Alan Nathan Kline was born on May 25, 1971, in [[Tiffin, Ohio]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/k/klin00200.html | title=Alan Kline | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=22 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Columbian High School]] in Tiffin.<ref name="Pfa"/>

Kline was a member of the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] from 1990 to 1993.<ref name="Pfa"/>  He was named first-team All-[[Big Ten]] by the [[Associated Press]] his sophomore year in 1991.<ref name=AP>{{cite news|title=Eight from 'M' All-Big Ten|newspaper=The Argus-Press (AP story)|date=November 26, 1991|page=14|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1988&dat=19911126&id=ZksiAAAAIBAJ&sjid=y6kFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1792,1954566&hl=en}}</ref> He started 37 games during his college career.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/81441/cid/5781994/1994-Signature-Rookies-28-Alan-Kline | title=#28 - Alan Kline PR45000 - Ohio State Buckeyes | publisher=tcdb.com | accessdate=22 December 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1994 NFL draft]], Kline signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] on May 2.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 28 and signed to the Saints' practice squad on August 30.<ref name="transactions"/> He was promoted to the active roster on December 22, 1994, but did not play in any games for the team during the 1994 season.<ref name="transactions"/> In 1995, Kline was allocated to the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF) to play for the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]] during the [[1995 WLAF season]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He later appeared in three games for the Saints during the [[1995 NFL season]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KlinAl20.htm | title=Alan Kline | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=22 December 2024}}</ref> He was released on August 25, 1996.<ref name="transactions"/>

Kline was signed by the [[New York Giants]] on March 20, 1997.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 11, 1997.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/k/klin00200.html | title=Alan Kline NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=22 December 2024}}</ref>
